Mild extracellular acidic pH (6.5) potentiates channel activation by noxious heat and vanilloids, whereas acidic conditions (pH <6) directly activate the channel. Can be activated by endogenous compounds, including 12-hydroperoxytetraenoic acid and bradykinin. Acts as ionotropic endocannabinoid receptor with central neuromodulatory effects. Triggers a form of long-term depression (TRPV1-LTD) mediated by the endocannabinoid anandamine in the hippocampus and nucleus accumbens by affecting AMPA receptors endocytosis.

gene.name: TSC complex subunit 1
gene.function: Non-catalytic component of the TSC-TBC complex, a multiprotein complex that acts as a negative regulator of the canonical mTORC1 complex, an evolutionarily conserved central nutrient sensor that stimulates anabolic reactions and macromolecule biosynthesis to promote cellular biomass generation and growth. The TSC-TBC complex acts as a GTPase-activating protein (GAP) for the small GTPase RHEB, a direct activator of the protein kinase activity of mTORC1. In absence of nutrients, the TSC-TBC complex inhibits mTORC1, thereby preventing phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6 kinase (RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2) and EIF4EBP1 (4E-BP1) by the mTORC1 signaling. The TSC-TBC complex is inactivated in response to nutrients, relieving inhibition of mTORC1. Within the TSC-TBC complex, TSC1 stabilizes TSC2 and prevents TSC2 self-aggregation. Acts as a tumor suppressor. Involved in microtubule- mediated protein transport via its ability to regulate mTORC1 signaling (By similarity). Also acts as a co-chaperone for HSP90AA1 facilitating HSP90AA1 chaperoning of protein clients such as kinases, TSC2 and glucocorticoid receptor NR3C1. Increases ATP binding to HSP90AA1 and inhibits HSP90AA1 ATPase activity. Competes with the activating co-chaperone AHSA1 for binding to HSP90AA1, thereby providing a reciprocal regulatory mechanism for chaperoning of client proteins. Recruits TSC2 to HSP90AA1 and stabilizes TSC2 by preventing the interaction between TSC2 and ubiquitin ligase HERC1.

gene.name: TSC complex subunit 2
gene.function: Catalytic component of the TSC-TBC complex, a multiprotein complex that acts as a negative regulator of the canonical mTORC1 complex, an evolutionarily conserved central nutrient sensor that stimulates anabolic reactions and macromolecule biosynthesis to promote cellular biomass generation and growth. Within the TSC-TBC complex, TSC2 acts as a GTPase- activating protein (GAP) for the small GTPase RHEB, a direct activator of the protein kinase activity of mTORC1. In absence of nutrients, the TSC-TBC complex inhibits mTORC1, thereby preventing phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6 kinase (RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2) and EIF4EBP1 (4E-BP1) by the mTORC1 signaling. The TSC-TBC complex is inactivated in response to nutrients, relieving inhibition of mTORC1. Involved in microtubule-mediated protein transport via its ability to regulate mTORC1 signaling (By similarity). Also stimulates the intrinsic GTPase activity of the Ras- related proteins RAP1A and RAB5 (By similarity).

gene.name: vascular endothelial growth factor A
gene.function: Participates in the induction of key genes involved in the response to hypoxia and in the induction of angiogenesis such as HIF1A. Involved in protecting cells from hypoxia- mediated cell death (By similarity).

phenotype.definition: Behavior or an act aimed at harming a person, animal, or physical property (e.g., acts of physical violence; shouting, swearing, and using harsh language; slashing someone's tires).
Angiofibroma consist of many often dilated vessels.

Intense feelings of nervousness, tension, or panic often arise in response to interpersonal stresses. There is worry about the negative effects of past unpleasant experiences and future negative possibilities. Individuals may feel fearful, apprehensive, or threatened by uncertainty, and they may also have fears of falling apart or losing control.

Any cardiac rhythm other than the normal sinus rhythm. Such a rhythm may be either of sinus or ectopic origin and either regular or irregular. An arrhythmia may be due to a disturbance in impulse formation or conduction or both.

Ataxia refers to impaired coordination of voluntary muscle movement. Cerebellar ataxia refers to ataxia due to dysfunction of the cerebellum. This causes a variety of elementary neurological deficits including asynergy (lack of coordination between muscles, limbs and joints), dysmetria (lack of ability to judge distances that can lead to under- or overshoot in grasping movements), and dysdiadochokinesia (inability to perform rapid movements requiring antagonizing muscle groups to be switched on and off repeatedly).

Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) manifests at age 2-3 years or by first grade at the latest. The main symptoms are distractibility, impulsivity, hyperactivity, and often trouble organizing tasks and projects, difficulty going to sleep, and social problems from being aggressive, loud, or impatient.
A reduced number of hematopoietic cells present in the bone marrow relative to marrow fat.
A benign tumor of cardiac striated muscle.
Accumulation of excessive amounts of lymphatic fluid (chyle) in the pleural cavity.
Abnormal cognition is characterized by deficits in thinking, reasoning, or remembering.
The presence of developmental dysplasia of the cerebral cortex.

Cortical tubers in the brain are hamartomatous lesions typically located at the gray-white matter interface, commonly in the frontal and parietal lobes. Cortical tubers are composed of abnormal glial and neural cells, and the size, number, and location vary among patients.
Abnormally increased frequency (usually defined as three or more) loose or watery bowel movements a day.
Abnormal feeling of sleepiness or difficulty staying awake.

A sudden flexion, extension, or mixed extension-flexion of predominantly proximal and truncal muscles that is usually more sustained than a myoclonic movement but not as sustained as a tonic seizure. Limited forms may occur: Grimacing, head nodding, or subtle eye movements. Epileptic spasms frequently occur in clusters. Infantile spasms are the best known form, but spasms can occur at all ages
Redness of the skin, caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.
phenotype.lay: Redness of skin or mucous membrane

phenotype.definition: A type of malformation of cortical development that primarily affects areas of neocortex. It can be identified on conventional magnetic resonance imaging as focal cortical thickening, abnormal gyration, and blurring between gray and white matter, often associated with clusters of heterotopic neurons.

Hydrocephalus is an active distension of the ventricular system of the brain resulting from inadequate passage of CSF from its point of production within the cerebral ventricles to its point of absorption into the systemic circulation.
phenotype.lay: Too much cerebrospinal fluid in the brain

phenotype.definition: A white or lighter patch of skin that may appear anywhere on the body and are caused by decreased skin pigmentation.

Hypsarrhythmia is abnormal interictal high amplitude waves and a background of irregular spikes. There is continuous (during wakefulness), high-amplitude (>200 Hz), generalized polymorphic slowing with no organized background and multifocal spikes demonstrated by electroencephalography (EEG).

Acting on the spur of the moment or on a momentary basis without consideration of outcomes; having difficulty establishing or following plans; experiencing a sense of urgency and engaging in behavior that is uninhibited, cannot be inhibited, and is uncontrolled. The possibility of repression is inconceivable.
Infantile spasms represent a subset of "epileptic spasms". Infantile Spasms are epileptic spasms starting in the first year of life (infancy).

The term intellectual disability or intellectual developmental disorder is used to describe significantly sub-average intellectual and adaptive functioning based on clinical assessment and as measured by individually administered, appropriately normed, standardized and validated tests of intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior, with onset during the developmental period from infancy through adolescence.
A benign liver neoplasm composed of fat, vascular, and smooth muscle elements.
Diffuse enlargement of the entire cerebral hemispheres leading to macrocephaly (with or without overlying cortical dysplasia).
The presence of many cysts in the kidney.
Accumulation of substantial excess body fat.
A clinically observable or self-reported abnormal behavior, experience, or physiological event that occurs in association with sleep, specific sleep stages, or sleep-wake transitions.
A neurofibroma in which Schwann cells proliferate inside the nerve sheath, producing an irregularly thickened, distorted, tortuous structure.
Increased levels of protein in the urine.

Infiltration of smooth muscle-like cells in lymph vessels as well as the lung (pleura, alveolar septa, bronchi, pulmonary vessels and lymphatics as well as lymph nodes, especially in posterior mediastinum and retroperitoneum). Focal emphysema can develop because of airway narrowing, and the thoracic duct may be obliterated. Pulmonary lymphangiomyomatosis may lead to multiple small cysts with a hamartomatous proliferation of smooth muscle in their walls.
A benign renal neoplasm composed of fat, vascular, and smooth muscle elements.
A hamartoma (a benign, focal malformation consisting of a disorganized mixture of cells and tissues) of the retina.

A seizure is an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterized by a transient occurrence of signs and/or symptoms due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain.
Self-aggression.

A plaque representing a connective-tissue nevus. Connective tissue naevi are uncommon skin lesions that occur when the deeper layers of the skin do not develop correctly or the components of these layers occur in the wrong proportion. Shagreen patches are oval-shaped and nevoid, skin-colored or occasionally pigmented, smooth or crinkled. The word shagreen refers to a type of roughened untanned leather.
A deficit in the retention of pieces of information (memory chunks) for a relatively short time (usually up to 30 seconds).
An abnormal pattern in the quality, quantity, or characteristics of sleep.
Stomatitis is an inflammation of the mucous membranes of any of the structures in the mouth.

A demarcated, largely intraventricular tumor in the region of the foramen of Monro composed of spindle to large plump or ganglion-like cells with eosinophilic to amphophilic cytoplasm and somewhat pleomorphic nuclei with occasional prominent nucleoli. These tumors are almost always associated with tuberous sclerosis.
Small nodular masses which originate in the subependymal region of the lateral ventricles and protrude into the ventricular cavity. They may represent subependymal hamartomas of tuberous sclerosis.

A vestibular schwannoma (also known as acoustic neuroma, acoustic neurinoma, or acoustic neurilemoma) is a benign, usually slow-growing tumor that develops from the VIIIth cranial nerve supplying the inner ear.

papers.title: Everolimus long-term use in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex: Four-year update of the EXIST-2 study.
papers.summary: The four-year EXIST-2 update found that everolimus produced sustained responses in renal angiomyolipoma, skin lesions, and subependymal giant cell astrocytomas, with few angiomyolipoma-related bleeding events and generally stable renal function. Treatment was associated with frequent adverse events, dose interruptions or reductions, and slight declines in pulmonary function among patients with lymphangioleiomyomatosis, so its overall benefit-risk profile was considered favorable but not free of limitations.
papers.why: Long-term randomized-extension follow-up demonstrates sustained efficacy and safety of everolimus for tuberous sclerosis–associated renal angiomyolipoma and other lesions.

papers.title: Multicenter phase 2 trial of sirolimus for tuberous sclerosis: kidney angiomyolipomas and other tumors regress and VEGF- D levels decrease.
papers.summary: This phase 2 clinical trial found that sirolimus regressed kidney, liver, and subependymal giant cell astrocytomas in adults with tuberous sclerosis, while responses generally required continued treatment and were associated with common toxicities. Serum VEGF-D decreased during treatment and correlated with kidney angiomyolipoma size, supporting its potential as a monitoring biomarker.
papers.why: A phase II trial provides direct evidence that sirolimus regresses TSC-associated tumors and that serum VEGF-D can monitor angiomyolipoma burden.

papers.title: The efficacy and safety of topical rapamycin-calcitriol for facial angiofibromas in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex: a prospective, double-blind, randomized clinical trial.
papers.summary: In a prospective, double-blind, randomized split-face trial of 52 patients with tuberous sclerosis complex, topical rapamycin-calcitriol ointment significantly reduced facial angiofibroma severity by week 12. Compared with rapamycin alone, the combination produced faster improvement in erythema, greater reduction in papule elevation, and longer durability after discontinuation, and all treatments were well tolerated.
papers.why: A randomized trial directly shows that topical rapamycin, calcitriol, and their combination improve TSC-related facial angiofibromas.

papers.title: Add-on Cannabidiol Treatment for Drug-Resistant Seizures in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex: A Placebo-Controlled Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: In a 16-week, double-blind randomized clinical trial, add-on cannabidiol at 25 or 50 mg/kg/day reduced treatment-resistant TSC-associated seizure frequency more than placebo, with similar efficacy between doses. Cannabidiol 25 mg/kg/day had a better safety profile than 50 mg/kg/day, while adverse events included diarrhea, somnolence, decreased appetite, and elevated liver transaminases.
papers.why: A phase III randomized trial directly showed that adjunctive cannabidiol significantly reduces medication-resistant seizures in tuberous sclerosis.

papers.title: Medical cannabinoids: a pharmacology-based systematic review and meta-analysis for all relevant medical indications.
papers.summary: The paper identifies cannabidiol as a therapy approved in the United States and Europe for seizures associated with tuberous sclerosis complex. It also reports high-grade evidence from randomized trials that cannabidiol reduces seizure frequency across epilepsy indications, although the pooled result is not presented specifically for tuberous sclerosis complex.
papers.why: The meta-analysis provides efficacy and safety data for cannabinoid drugs in epilepsy and spasticity, phenotypes and therapeutic areas that can transfer to TSC.

papers.title: Estradiol and mTORC2 cooperate to enhance prostaglandin biosynthesis and tumorigenesis in TSC2-deficient LAM cells.
papers.summary: The paper shows that loss of TSC2 creates a rapamycin-insensitive, mTORC2/Rictor-dependent increase in COX-2 and prostaglandin production that is further enhanced by estradiol. COX-2 inhibition reduced proliferation or tumor development in Tsc2-deficient models, and LAM patients exhibited COX-2-rich pulmonary lesions and elevated serum prostaglandins, supporting transfer of this pathway as a potential therapeutic target from LAM to TSC-related disease.
papers.why: The study identifies COX-2/prostaglandin pathway targeting with celecoxib or aspirin as having therapeutic effects in TSC2-deficient LAM models and links pathway activity to measurable biomarkers.

papers.title: [Arrhythmia as the first symptom of neonatal cardiac tumors: Case report].
papers.journal: Rev Med Inst Mex Seguro Soc
papers.summary: This case report describes a male newborn with multiple cardiac rhabdomyomas presenting with supraventricular extrasystoles and conduction-system involvement. Combined propranolol and everolimus treatment was associated with rapid reduction of ectopy, resolution of the tumors within eight weeks, and no recurrence of arrhythmia or masses at 12 months.
papers.why: A neonatal case associated with tuberous sclerosis reports arrhythmia control with everolimus plus propranolol and resolution of multiple cardiac rhabdomyomas.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of six new antiseizure medications for adjunctive treatment of focal epilepsy and epileptic syndrome: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and network meta-analysis found that high-exposure everolimus was the most effective evaluated adjunctive treatment strategy for tuberous sclerosis complex among the six antiseizure medications compared. The finding was based on indirect treatment rankings and requires further confirmation.
papers.why: The systematic review and network meta-analysis compare six antiseizure medications, including everolimus and cannabidiol, using efficacy and safety outcomes relevant to TSC.

papers.title: Enhanced Sestrin expression through Tanshinone 2A treatment improves PI3K-dependent inhibition of glioma growth.
papers.summary: The paper shows that Tanshinone 2A rapidly inhibits PI3K/PKB signaling and, after prolonged exposure, suppresses mTORC1 activity in Dictyostelium discoideum through increased Sestrin expression independently of PKB, TSC2, and AMPK. Tanshinone 2A combined with the PI3K inhibitor Paxalisib synergistically inhibited glioblastoma cell proliferation and spheroid expansion, but no tuberous sclerosis models or patients were studied, so relevance to tuberous sclerosis is mechanistic rather than directly demonstrated.
papers.why: The study experimentally identifies a sestrin-dependent mechanism for Tanshinone IIA and shows synergistic mTOR/PI3K-pathway suppression with paxalisib, offering a transferable preclinical strategy.

papers.title: Progress report on new epilepsy treatments: A summary of the Eighteenth Eilat Conference on New Antiepileptic Drugs and Devices (EILAT XVIII). II. Treatments in more advanced clinical development.
papers.summary: The paper reviews investigational epilepsy treatments and states that radiprodil is in development for seizures and other symptoms associated with tuberous sclerosis complex, as well as GRIN-related neurodevelopmental disorder and focal cortical dysplasia type II. It describes radiprodil as a negative allosteric modulator that binds the GluN2B subunit of the NMDA receptor, but provides no preliminary seizure-outcome results for tuberous sclerosis complex in the abstract.
papers.why: The conference report summarizes preliminary clinical development data for radiprodil explicitly being investigated for seizures and symptoms associated with tuberous sclerosis complex.

papers.title: Management of lymphangioleiomyomatosis.
papers.summary: This review identifies TSC1/TSC2 loss and consequent mTOR pathway activation as mechanistic links between lymphangioleiomyomatosis and tuberous sclerosis complex. It reports that sirolimus and everolimus inhibit mTORC1 and improve selected clinical, animal, and cellular outcomes, while combinations targeting autophagy, RhoA, VEGF signaling, or other pathways remain investigational or have mixed preclinical results.
papers.why: The review reports established and investigational mTOR-directed treatments for LAM, a major TSC-associated manifestation, including tested combination strategies.

papers.title: Autistic-like behaviour and cerebellar dysfunction in Purkinje cell Tsc1 mutant mice.
papers.summary: In Purkinje cell-specific Tsc1 mutant mice, loss of Tsc1 increased mTOR signaling, reduced Purkinje cell number and excitability, and produced autistic-like behavioral abnormalities, even before overt cell loss. Starting at postnatal day 7, the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin prevented the major pathological and behavioral deficits, supporting TSC–mTOR signaling as a therapeutic target in this model.
papers.why: This study establishes a TSC1-related mouse model with autism-like phenotypes and shows that rapamycin prevents behavioral and cerebellar deficits.

papers.title: TSC-mTOR maintains quiescence and function of hematopoietic stem cells by repressing mitochondrial biogenesis and reactive oxygen species.
papers.summary: Conditional Tsc1 deletion in adult mouse HSCs activated mTOR, drove loss of quiescence, increased mitochondrial biogenesis and reactive oxygen species, and impaired long-term hematopoietic stem-cell function. Rapamycin and the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine substantially rescued the hematopoietic defects, supporting reactive oxygen species as a major downstream mediator of TSC–mTOR-dependent HSC dysfunction.
papers.why: A Tsc1-deficient hematopoietic model provides direct disease-gene evidence that ROS antagonism can rescue stem-cell numbers and function.

papers.title: Tuberous sclerosis complex surveillance and management: recommendations of the 2012 International Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Consensus Conference.
papers.summary: This consensus statement provides evidence-graded surveillance, diagnostic, and management recommendations for tuberous sclerosis complex across the lifespan. It identifies the TSC1/TSC2–Rheb–mTORC1 mechanism and summarizes clinical use of mTOR inhibitors, vigabatrin, surgery, imaging, neurophysiologic testing, and multisystem monitoring, while emphasizing limited evidence for treatment of TSC-associated neuropsychiatric disorders.
papers.why: The paper provides an evidence-based, standardized surveillance and management framework reusable across the full TSC disease course.

papers.title: Lung-selective mRNA delivery of synthetic lipid nanoparticles for the treatment of pulmonary lymphangioleiomyomatosis.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: The study develops amide-linker N-series lipid nanoparticles that preferentially deliver mRNA to mouse lungs, with the hybrid 306-N16B/306-O12B formulation delivering wild-type mouse Tsc2 mRNA to TSC2-deficient TTJ tumor cells. Tsc2 mRNA restored TSC2 activity, suppressed mTORC1 signaling, reduced proliferation and tumor burden, and increased T-cell infiltration in a preclinical mouse model of pulmonary lymphangioleiomyomatosis, without evidence yet from human patients.
papers.why: The study demonstrates lung-selective mRNA delivery and Tsc2 restoration that reduces tumor burden in a preclinical TSC2-related LAM model.

papers.title: mTORC1 drives HIF-1α and VEGF-A signalling via multiple mechanisms involving 4E-BP1, S6K1 and STAT3.
papers.summary: The paper shows that rapamycin reduces HIF-1α and, less strongly, VEGF-A expression in renal cystadenomas from Tsc2+/− mice. Mechanistic experiments indicate that mTORC1 promotes HIF-1α synthesis through STAT3-dependent transcription and 4E-BP1/eIF4E- and S6K1-dependent translation, while VEGF-A expression is primarily controlled by the 4E-BP1/eIF4E arm.
papers.why: Rapamycin treatment experiments in a Tsc2 mouse model demonstrate suppression of tumor-relevant HIF-1α and VEGF-A signaling through mTORC1.

papers.title: Mosaic and Intronic Mutations in TSC1/TSC2 Explain the Majority of TSC Patients with No Mutation Identified by Conventional Testing.
papers.summary: Comprehensive next-generation sequencing of TSC1 and TSC2 identified causal mutations in 45 of 53 patients with tuberous sclerosis complex previously classified as having no mutation identified, primarily revealing mosaic and intronic variants. Analysis of TSC-related skin tumors increased detection, while high-depth sequencing of complete genes and flanking intronic regions was recommended for sensitive mutation detection.
papers.why: The study demonstrates a high-yield diagnostic strategy using full-coverage NGS, parental samples, and tumor biopsies for mutation-negative TSC.

papers.title: Rapamycin reverses impaired social interaction in mouse models of tuberous sclerosis complex.
papers.summary: In Tsc1+/− and Tsc2+/− mice, reduced social interaction and increased rearing were associated with dysregulated, rapamycin-sensitive mTOR signalling. Short-term rapamycin treatment normalized social interaction, attenuated rearing, and suppressed S6K phosphorylation in adult mice, supporting mTOR inhibition as a potential treatment for autism-related social impairment in tuberous sclerosis complex.
papers.why: Rapamycin treatment reversed impaired social interaction in a mouse model of TSC, supporting mTOR inhibition for TSC-associated autistic behavior.

papers.title: Loss of Tsc2 in radial glia models the brain pathology of tuberous sclerosis complex in the mouse.
papers.summary: Selective loss of Tsc2 in radial glial progenitor cells produced a mouse model with mTORC1 activation, abnormal neural progenitor differentiation, neuronal migration defects, astrogliosis, enlarged neural and glial cells, and impaired myelination. Although the model reproduced several neuropathologic features of tuberous sclerosis complex, focal cortical tubers were absent, and rapamycin was proposed for future testing rather than evaluated in these mice.
papers.why: This conditional Tsc2 knockout mouse reproduces major cortical and hippocampal lesions and mTORC1 activation relevant to TSC brain research.

papers.title: TSC-associated neuropsychiatric disorders (TAND): findings from the TOSCA natural history study.
papers.summary: The TOSCA international natural history registry characterized the frequency, age pattern, and genotype associations of tuberous sclerosis-associated neuropsychiatric disorders (TAND) in 2216 participants. It found a large neuropsychiatric burden, more overactivity and impulsivity in children, more anxiety and depressive manifestations in adults, and several TAND phenotypes more frequent in participants with TSC2 than TSC1 mutations, while extensive missing data and clinical ascertainment bias limited interpretation.
papers.why: Provides large-scale longitudinal characterization of neuropsychiatric phenotypes and clinical outcomes in TSC, useful for natural-history studies and trial endpoint selection.

papers.title: Purkinje cells derived from TSC patients display hypoexcitability and synaptic deficits associated with reduced FMRP levels and reversed by rapamycin.
papers.summary: The paper establishes patient-derived TSC2-mutant hiPSC Purkinje cell cultures as an in vitro model of tuberous sclerosis and shows mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired differentiation, abnormal morphology, synaptic deficits, and hypoexcitability. Rapamycin and Torin1 partially or substantially reverse these cellular abnormalities in vitro, but effects on patient cerebellar volume or neurological symptoms remain untested predictions.
papers.why: Patient-derived TSC2-mutant Purkinje cells provide a disease-specific neuronal model in which rapamycin reverses differentiation, synaptic, and excitability abnormalities.

papers.title: Whole Exome Sequencing Identifies TSC1/TSC2 Biallelic Loss as the Primary and Sufficient Driver Event for Renal Angiomyolipoma Development.
papers.summary: Whole-exome analysis of 30 renal angiomyolipomas and 2 LAM lesions found that biallelic loss of TSC2 or, less commonly, TSC1 was the predominant recurrent driver event, with few other somatic mutations and no recurrent pathway enrichment. These genomic findings support targeting consequences of TSC1/TSC2 loss, particularly mTORC1 activation, while reported rapamycin responses were often long-lasting but complete responses were virtually unknown and partial responses rare.
papers.why: Whole-exome analysis of TSC-associated tumors directly identifies biallelic TSC1/TSC2 loss and supplies a reusable method for characterizing renal angiomyolipoma and LAM tissue.

papers.title: Epilepsy in the mTORopathies: opportunities for precision medicine.
papers.summary: This review identifies hyperactivation of mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) as a central epileptogenic mechanism in tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) and supports mTORC1 inhibition as a targeted treatment strategy. Clinical evidence shows that everolimus reduces drug-resistant seizures in TSC, while vigabatrin, tuberectomy, genetic testing, therapeutic drug monitoring, and selected rapalogues provide additional research or clinical resources relevant to TSC management.
papers.why: The review presents everolimus efficacy in TSC and a transferable precision-medicine framework combining pathogenic mTOR-pathway variant identification with targeted therapy.

papers.title: Topical rapamycin therapy to alleviate the cutaneous manifestations of tuberous sclerosis complex: a double-blind, randomized, controlled trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of topically applied rapamycin.
papers.summary: The paper reports a prospective randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of topical low-dose rapamycin for facial angiofibromas in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex. Subjective improvement was reported more often with rapamycin than placebo, but the study was not powered for statistical significance; no detectable systemic absorption or significant complete-blood-count changes were observed.
papers.why: A randomized controlled trial in TSC shows that topical rapamycin safely reduces the appearance of facial angiofibromas without detectable systemic absorption.

papers.title: Neuronal CTGF/CCN2 negatively regulates myelination in a mouse model of tuberous sclerosis complex.
papers.summary: The study identifies neuronal CTGF/CCN2 as a non-cell-autonomous mediator of hypomyelination in Tsc1-deficient mice: neuronal Tsc1 loss elevates CTGF, suppresses oligodendrocyte maturation, and reduces myelination. Rapamycin reverses the molecular and myelin defects, while neuronal Ctgf deletion improves the number of myelinated axons but does not restore myelin thickness or oligodendrocyte numbers in white matter.
papers.why: The study provides a TSC mouse model and demonstrates that neuronal CTGF deletion rescues TSC-related hypomyelination, identifying a concrete therapeutic avenue.

papers.title: Highly Purified Cannabidiol for Epilepsy Treatment: A Systematic Review of Epileptic Conditions Beyond Dravet Syndrome and Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome.
papers.summary: This systematic review found that pharmaceutical-grade cannabidiol reduced seizure frequency in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex, with the highest-quality evidence coming from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Open-label evidence additionally suggested responses in refractory epileptic spasms, but treatment requires monitoring for adverse effects and clinically important interactions with clobazam, valproic acid, and mechanistic target of rapamycin inhibitors.
papers.why: The systematic review reports randomized-trial evidence that purified CBD reduces seizure frequency in TSC and documents a concrete approved or investigational treatment solution.

papers.title: Long-term cannabidiol treatment for seizures in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex: An open-label extension trial.
papers.summary: In the open-label extension of GWPCARE6, add-on cannabidiol reduced TSC-associated and total seizure frequencies through 48 weeks and was associated with global improvement in most assessed patients. Adverse events were common but generally mild or moderate, while liver-transaminase elevations and permanent discontinuations identified important safety-monitoring considerations, especially with concomitant valproate.
papers.why: The open-label extension provides patient data showing sustained seizure reduction and global improvement with long-term add-on cannabidiol in TSC.

papers.title: Epileptogenesis in tuberous sclerosis complex-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
papers.summary: This review concludes that tuberous sclerosis complex epileptogenesis is a dynamic process involving TSC1/TSC2-associated mTORC1 hyperactivation, altered excitation–inhibition balance, and both neuronal and non-neuronal mechanisms that also contribute to neurodevelopmental comorbidity. It identifies mTOR inhibition, particularly everolimus, as clinically effective for TSC-associated epilepsy, while highlighting limited or null effects on autism and intellectual disability and the need for predictive biomarkers and earlier, stage-specific treatment.
papers.why: The review summarizes clinically tested interventions for TSC-associated epileptogenesis, including vigabatrin and everolimus, with evidence supporting early mTOR-directed treatment.

papers.title: Rapamycin weekly maintenance dosing and the potential efficacy of combination sorafenib plus rapamycin but not atorvastatin or doxycycline in tuberous sclerosis preclinical models.
papers.summary: In Tsc2 mouse models, prolonged intermittent rapamycin exposure markedly reduced kidney cystadenoma burden, whereas adding interferon-gamma, atorvastatin, or doxycycline provided no additional benefit. Adding sorafenib to rapamycin modestly improved survival in a subcutaneous Tsc2-null tumor model, but sorafenib alone was ineffective, supporting further study of combined mTOR and VEGF-pathway inhibition.
papers.why: The Tsc2-deficient mouse study provides direct evidence for durable rapamycin dosing and tests combination strategies against TSC kidney tumors.

papers.title: A cross-syndrome cohort comparison of sleep disturbance in children with Smith-Magenis syndrome, Angelman syndrome, autism spectrum disorder and tuberous sclerosis complex.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional observational study, children with tuberous sclerosis complex had greater night waking, parasomnia, and daytime sleepiness scores than chronologically age-matched typically developing children, but no single sleep profile was specific to TSC. In TSC, poorer health and symptoms indicative of gastro-oesophageal reflux were associated with several sleep disturbances, whereas age, recent seizures, obesity, and daytime drowsiness showed no significant relationships with the measured sleep outcomes.
papers.why: The study applies a standardized sleep-disturbance assessment to TSC and other neurodevelopmental disorders, generating syndrome-specific outcome profiles and associations.

papers.title: Management of everolimus-associated adverse events in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex: a practical guide.
papers.summary: This practical review reports that everolimus has demonstrated clinical benefit in tuberous sclerosis complex, particularly for renal angiomyolipoma and subependymal giant astrocytoma, while sirolimus has also shown efficacy for angiomyolipoma and lymphangioleiomyomatosis. It emphasizes that adverse events are common but often manageable through monitoring, supportive care, dose reduction, or temporary interruption, allowing most patients to continue treatment.
papers.why: This practical guide provides an existing clinical framework for managing toxicities and treatment interruptions while maintaining everolimus benefits in TSC.

papers.title: Regulation of PERK-eIF2α signalling by tuberous sclerosis complex-1 controls homoeostasis and survival of myelinating oligodendrocytes.
papers.summary: This study shows that oligodendrocyte-lineage Tsc1 deletion in mice activates mTOR and PERK–eIF2α-dependent endoplasmic-reticulum stress, alongside Fas–JNK apoptotic signaling, causing oligodendrocyte loss and severe CNS hypomyelination. Rapamycin improved some differentiation and myelination outcomes, whereas guanabenz, which enhances eIF2α phosphorylation by inhibiting Gadd34–PP1 activity, reduced oligodendrocyte death and partially restored myelination in Tsc1-mutant cells and mice.
papers.why: The paper reports that guanabenz enhances eIF2α stress adaptation, protects oligodendrocytes, and partially rescues myelination defects in a TSC1 mutant mouse model.

papers.title: mTOR inhibitors in the pharmacologic management of tuberous sclerosis complex and their potential role in other rare neurodevelopmental disorders.
papers.summary: This review concludes that mTOR inhibition with sirolimus or everolimus has substantial clinical evidence for several tuberous sclerosis complex manifestations, particularly subependymal giant cell astrocytoma and renal angiomyolipoma, with emerging evidence for seizures. The same pathway is implicated in Leigh syndrome, Down syndrome, and neurofibromatosis types 1 and 2, but transfer evidence remains predominantly preclinical, mixed, or negative in selected clinical studies.
papers.why: This review summarizes clinical evidence for mTOR inhibitors in tuberous sclerosis complex and their potential effects on seizures, tumors, renal disease, and other manifestations.

papers.title: Mutations causing syndromic autism define an axis of synaptic pathophysiology.
papers.summary: In Tsc2+/− mice, reduced rather than increased mGluR-dependent hippocampal protein synthesis produced deficient mGluR-LTD and impaired context discrimination. Acute rapamycin or the mGluR5 positive allosteric modulator CDPPB restored these deficits, while combining Tsc2 and Fmr1 mutations normalized mGluR-LTD and memory, demonstrating opposite but interactive synaptic pathophysiology in TSC and fragile X syndrome.
papers.why: Mouse experiments show that opposing mGluR5-modulating treatments correct synaptic, biochemical, and cognitive defects in TSC-related and fragile X models.

papers.title: Chronic signaling via the metabolic checkpoint kinase mTORC1 induces macrophage granuloma formation and marks sarcoidosis progression.
papers.summary: The paper shows that loss of Tsc2 in myeloid cells activates mTORC1, drives macrophage hypertrophy, proliferation, metabolic reprogramming, and granuloma formation, and that mTORC1 inhibition with everolimus reverses established granulomas in mice. These findings also associate mTORC1 activation, macrophage proliferation, and glycolysis with progressive human sarcoidosis, providing a mechanistically relevant model and therapeutic strategy that may be transferable to granulomatous manifestations of tuberous sclerosis, although tuberculosis/sclerosis patients were not studied directly.
papers.why: TSC2-deficient macrophages and sarcoidosis share a mechanistic mTORC1 axis with TSC, and the study provides an in vivo model plus evidence that mTORC1 inhibition can resolve TSC2-associated granulomas.

papers.title: Sirolimus therapy for fetal cardiac rhabdomyoma in a pregnant woman with tuberous sclerosis.
papers.summary: In a pregnant woman with tuberous sclerosis carrying a pathogenic TSC2 variant, oral sirolimus was associated with complete radiographic disappearance of multiple fetal cardiac rhabdomyomas after maternal and fetal drug exposure reached therapeutic levels. The case supports sirolimus as a potential prenatal therapy, but the single-patient evidence and acknowledged uncertainty about pregnancy safety and optimal dosing prevent firm efficacy or safety conclusions.
papers.why: This case reports complete in utero resolution of a fetal cardiac rhabdomyoma in a pregnant woman with TSC during sirolimus treatment.

papers.title: Reduced juvenile long-term depression in tuberous sclerosis complex is mitigated in adults by compensatory recruitment of mGluR5 and Erk signaling.
papers.summary: In adult TSC2+/− mice, compensatory elevation of hippocampal mGluR5 expression and Erk phosphorylation restores the magnitude of long-term depression but makes it insensitive to mTORC1 inhibition. Pharmacological antagonism of mGluR5 or Mek-Erk signaling restores mTOR dependence, suppresses DHPG-induced CA3 epileptiform bursting, and eliminates a perseverative behavioral phenotype.
papers.why: Using TSC2-mutant mice and hippocampal slices, the study identifies stage-specific mGluR5-Erk pathway modulation that reduces epileptiform activity and perseverative behavior.

papers.title: The therapeutic potential of purified cannabidiol.
papers.summary: The review reports that purified cannabidiol oral solution (Epidiolex) is approved to manage seizures in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex, supported by multiple positive phase 3 randomized controlled trials. It reports an average seizure reduction of approximately 50% at typical doses of 20–25 mg/kg/day.
papers.why: The review explicitly identifies purified cannabidiol as an approved treatment for seizures in tuberous sclerosis complex and discusses clinical evidence supporting its use.

papers.title: Self-injury and aggression in tuberous sclerosis complex: cross syndrome comparison and associated risk markers.
papers.summary: This observational study found high reported rates of self-injury (27%) and aggression (50%) among 37 children with tuberous sclerosis complex, although the rates were not significantly different from those in comparison syndrome groups, particularly Down syndrome. Self-injury and aggression were associated with lower mood or adaptive functioning and with greater activity, repetitive or autistic-symptom behaviors, and behavioral indicators of pain, but the observational design does not establish causation.
papers.why: This study provides validated behavioral assessment tools and identifies measurable risk markers for self-injury and aggression in children with TSC.

papers.title: Review of the treatment options for epilepsy in tuberous sclerosis complex: towards precision medicine.
papers.summary: This review summarizes precision treatments for tuberous sclerosis complex-associated epilepsy, emphasizing preventive intervention during epileptogenesis. Everolimus, cannabidiol, vigabatrin, ketogenic diets, vagus nerve stimulation, and selected surgery reduce seizures in selected populations, but neuropsychiatric benefit is uncertain and developmental mTOR inhibition may pose safety risks.
papers.why: This review summarizes clinically tested and preventative treatments for TSC-associated epilepsy, including mTOR-targeted drugs, cannabidiol, ketogenic diet, neurostimulation, and surgery.

papers.title: TSC patient-derived isogenic neural progenitor cells reveal altered early neurodevelopmental phenotypes and rapamycin-induced MNK-eIF4E signaling.
papers.summary: Patient-derived isogenic TSC1 neural progenitor cell models revealed that heterozygous and homozygous loss of TSC1 produces increased cell size, mTORC1 signaling, proliferation, and neurite outgrowth, with genotype-dependent transcriptional changes. Rapamycin reversed the increased cell size and suppressed mTORC1, but did not improve proliferation or neurite outgrowth and instead increased MEK-ERK and MNK-eIF4E signaling, motivating combination treatment with MEK or MNK inhibitors.
papers.why: This study directly generates TSC1 patient-specific isogenic iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells, characterizes neurodevelopmental phenotypes, tests rapamycin response, and identifies pathway combinations for follow-up screening.

papers.title: MCP-1 overexpressed in tuberous sclerosis lesions acts as a paracrine factor for tumor development.
papers.summary: Cells derived from tuberous sclerosis skin tumors overexpressed MCP-1 relative to fibroblasts from the same patients' normal skin, and tumor-conditioned medium recruited monocytic cells through MCP-1-dependent chemotaxis rather than increasing fibroblast proliferation. In Tsc2-null rat embryonic fibroblasts, MCP-1 overexpression was suppressed by wild-type TSC2 or inhibitors of PI3K, Rheb, or mTOR signaling, identifying MCP-1 as a potential paracrine mediator and therapeutic target for TSC skin-tumor development.
papers.why: The study directly links TSC lesion cells and Tsc2-deficient fibroblasts to MCP-1 production and experimentally shows that neutralizing MCP-1 or inhibiting Rheb-mTOR suppresses tumor-associated chemotactic activity.

papers.title: Molecular analysis of TSC1 and TSC2 genes and phenotypic correlations in Brazilian families with tuberous sclerosis.
papers.summary: This Brazilian cohort study found germline TSC1 or TSC2 variants in 47 of 53 patients with tuberous sclerosis, including five large rearrangements and 45 point mutations, using MLPA, next-generation sequencing, and Sanger confirmation. The clinical testing strategy had an overall variant detection rate of 89%, while limited cohort size, incomplete segregation analysis, and multiple comparisons prevented establishment of reliable additional genotype-phenotype correlations.
papers.why: The study combines MLPA and a targeted sequencing panel to detect point mutations and large rearrangements in 47 of 53 suspected Brazilian TSC cases and relates genotype to phenotype.

papers.title: Downregulation of CD47 and CD200 in patients with focal cortical dysplasia type IIb and tuberous sclerosis complex.
papers.summary: In pediatric tuberous sclerosis cortical tubers, CD47, SIRP-α, and CD200 were downregulated at messenger RNA and protein levels, while CD200R was unchanged; lower CD47 and CD200 expression correlated with more activated microglia. Soluble CD47 Fc and CD200 Fc reduced IL-6 release in living TSC epileptogenic brain slices but did not suppress IL-1β or IL-17, supporting selective rather than broad anti-inflammatory activity in an ex vivo, descriptive model.
papers.why: Human TSC lesion tissue and live slices show downregulated immune-inhibitory pathways and selective cytokine suppression by soluble CD47 and CD200.

papers.title: Comparison of three rapamycin dosing schedules in A/J Tsc2+/- mice and improved survival with angiogenesis inhibitor or asparaginase treatment in mice with subcutaneous tuberous sclerosis related tumors.
papers.summary: In mouse models of TSC-related tumors, prolonged rapamycin treatment reduced kidney cystadenoma burden more effectively than high-intensity short courses, while single-agent asparaginase, sunitinib, and bevacizumab produced modest benefits in the Tsc2-/- subcutaneous tumor model. None of the tested non-mTOR agents improved outcomes when added to rapamycin, and vincristine was ineffective; the A/J Tsc2+/- mouse was identified as a higher-throughput model of TSC kidney disease.
papers.why: This study directly tests TSC2 mouse models, rapamycin schedules, angiogenesis inhibitors, and asparaginase against TSC-related tumors and reports quantitative efficacy outcomes.

papers.title: Phenotypic distinctions between mosaic forms of tuberous sclerosis complex.
papers.summary: This observational study stratifies mosaic tuberous sclerosis complex into symmetric- and asymmetric-facial-angiofibroma phenotypes and shows that asymmetric distribution is associated with fewer disease findings, later penetrance, lower blood variant allele fraction, and lower observed transmission to offspring. Affected skin and blood should be tested with next-generation sequencing because low-level mosaic TSC1/TSC2 variants can be missed by conventional blood testing, and mosaic patients can still have serious internal-organ disease.
papers.why: The study validates NGS-based molecular profiling and blood variant allele fraction as methods for identifying and stratifying mosaic tuberous sclerosis.

papers.title: Response to everolimus is seen in TSC-associated SEGAs and angiomyolipomas independent of mutation type and site in TSC1 and TSC2.
papers.summary: In the randomized EXIST-1 and EXIST-2 trials, everolimus reduced TSC-associated subependymal giant cell astrocytoma or renal angiomyolipoma burden in a substantial proportion of treated patients. Response was not detectably associated with TSC1 or TSC2 mutation type, location, truncating status, or the absence of an identified mutation.
papers.why: Data from EXIST-1 and EXIST-2 confirm that everolimus benefits TSC-associated SEGAs and angiomyolipomas regardless of TSC1/TSC2 mutation type or site.

papers.title: Myelin Pathology Beyond White Matter in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) Cortical Tubers.
papers.summary: Analysis of resected cortical tubers from 46 patients with tuberous sclerosis complex found reduced oligodendroglial numbers in both gray and white matter, myelin loss primarily in white matter, and loss of nodes of Ranvier without a reduction in axons. Reduced white-matter oligodendroglial numbers were associated with lower intelligence quotient, and reduced gray-matter myelin-associated oligodendrocyte basic protein was associated with autism-spectrum disorder/TSC-associated neuropsychiatric disorder, but the causal roles of mTOR activation, seizures, and immune cells remain unresolved.
papers.why: The study directly quantifies myelin and oligodendroglial abnormalities in TSC cortical tubers and links measurable tissue features with cognitive and autism phenotypes.

papers.title: Mutational analysis of TSC1 and TSC2 genes in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex patients from Greece.
papers.summary: Genetic testing of 20 unrelated Greek probands or families identified pathogenic TSC1 or TSC2 variants in 13 cases, including five previously unreported variants, with substantially higher detection among definite than possible TSC diagnoses. The clinical data suggested generally milder disease in TSC1-related TSC than in TSC2-related TSC, while sequence analysis, MLPA, transcript analysis, and structural modeling clarified or excluded the effects of several variants.
papers.why: Reports a molecular diagnostic workflow with sequencing and MLPA data from TSC patients, including mutation-detection rates and genotype-associated phenotypes.

papers.title: First comprehensive TSC1/TSC2 mutational analysis in Mexican patients with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex reveals numerous novel pathogenic variants.
papers.summary: A combined SSCP/Sanger sequencing, MLPA, and next-generation sequencing strategy identified a pathogenic or likely pathogenic TSC1 or TSC2 variant in 62 of 66 clinically definitive Mexican patients with tuberous sclerosis complex, identifying 40% previously unreported variants. In silico modeling predicted that two likely pathogenic variants could alter hamartin or tuberin structure, but the study did not establish a clear genotype–phenotype correlation and found no variant in three definitively diagnosed cases.
papers.why: Provides sequencing, rearrangement detection, and structural modeling approaches with high mutation yield in a large TSC cohort.

papers.title: Phase 1, Open-label, Drug-drug Interaction Study to Assess Effect Between Radiprodil and the Co-administered Drugs.
papers.summary: This is a Phase 1, open-label, 3-period study to determine radiprodil's potential to act as a perpetrator of cytochrome P-450 (CYP) metabolic pathways and transporter pathways. The study will evaluate the pharmacokinetics (PK) and safety effects of co-administration of radiprodil with oral midazolam, rosuvastatin, warfarin, digoxin, and omeprazole in healthy adult subjects. The study will be conducted in 1 cohort of healthy adult participants only.

papers.title: Rapamycin Therapy for Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex and Sporadic LAM
papers.summary: The purpose of this study was to determine if rapamycin reduced angiomyolipomata volume in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex or lam.

papers.title: Long Term Follow Up for RAD001 Therapy of Angiomyolipomata in Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis (TSC) and Sporadic Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM)
papers.summary:
This is an open label long term follow up study, open to those subjects who were previously enrolled in"RAD001 Therapy of Angiomyolipomata in Patients with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex and Sporadic Lymphangioleiomyomatosis", CCHMC IRB #2008-0812 and who meet the criteria for this long-term follow-up study.

The hypothesis is that the drug will inhibit the growth of the angiomyolipomas and possibly even cause regression.

papers.title: Sabril for Complex Partial Seizures in Adult Tolerability Study (TS) Patients
papers.summary:
This is an open-label, phase 4 study to examine the safety and efficacy of vigabatrin (Sabril) in Tuberous Sclerosis patients, a subset of the larger refractory complex partial epilepsy population for which the drug is approved. While enrolled on this trial, subjects will continue to take all of their normally prescribed medications, including their other antiepileptic drugs (AEDs).

Alternatively, there is a prospective observational arm that subjects who are about to take Sabril as treatment for seizures associated with Tuberous Sclerosis may join. Subjects who join this arm will not have an

papers.title: Trial of RAD001 and Neurocognition in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC)
papers.summary: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) is a multi-system disease, usually presenting with seizures, mental retardation and autism, and exhibiting a high variability in clinical findings both among and within families. Investigators are doing research in order to identify possible neurocognitive benefits from treatment with RAD001 or placebo for a six month period. There may also be potential for improvements in seizure frequency, sleep and autistic behaviors. We hope this trial will lead to a better understanding of TSC and to new forms of treatment, to benefit children and adults with TSC in the fu

papers.title: A Phase 2, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of TAK-935 (OV935) as an Adjunctive Therapy in Pediatric Participants With Developmental and/or Epileptic Encephalopathies
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the effect on the frequency of all seizures (convulsive and drop) in participants treated with TAK-935 compared to placebo.

papers.title: Study to Investigate LP352 in Subjects With Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies
papers.summary: The objective of this study is to assess the safety, tolerability, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of adjunctive therapy of LP352 in adults and adolescents with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.

papers.title: Long-term, Prospective Study Evaluating Clinical and Molecular Biomarkers of Epileptogenesis in a Genetic Model of Epilepsy - Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
papers.summary:
The primary objective of clinical part of EPISTOP project is to identify the clinical and molecular biomarkers of epileptogenesis in a prospective clinical study of patients with TSC.

Secondary objective of the clinical part of EPISTOP is to compare the effects of standard antiepileptic treatment in patients diagnosed as having epilepsy after clinical seizures vs after electroencephalographic epileptiform discharges, in a randomized trial in TSC patients.

papers.title: Everolimus (RAD001) Therapy for Epilepsy in Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC)
papers.summary: The goal of this study is to learn if the study drug RAD001 can reduced the number of epileptic seizures, and can be taken safety by people who have epilepsy associated with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.

papers.title: Open-label, Long-term Safety Study of LP352 in Subjects With Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
papers.summary: The objective of this study is to assess the long-term safety, tolerability, and efficacy of adjunctive therapy of LP352 in subjects with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies who completed participation in Study LP352-201.

papers.title: Aspirin as an add-on Treatment of Refractory Epilepsy in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
papers.summary: There had been much evidence in aspirin controlling tumorous conditions conducted by basic researches, especially through mammilian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway. The investigator observed efficacy of aspirin in the treatment of tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) in one child who got Kawasaki disease and in the addition four TSC patients with epilepsy. The investigator intend to evaluate whether aspirin would be an effective add-on treatment in TSC patients with refractory seizures.

papers.title: Everolimus (RAD001) Therapy of Giant Cell Astrocytoma in Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
papers.summary:
The purpose of the study is to evaluate the safety and potential side effects of everolimus (an experimental drug) on a person with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex who also has been diagnosed with a brain tumor (astrocytoma)

The hypothesis is that the drug will cause the tumor size to decrease, and may have beneficial activity separate from effects on tumors in patients.

papers.title: Safety of Simvastatin in LAM and TSC
papers.summary: The purpose of this research study is to see if simvastatin can be taken safely in patients with either LAM or TSC, who are already being treated with everolimus or sirolimus. This is the first step in looking at simvastatin as a drug that may help patients, by impacting the growth and survival of cells that make up the lung lesions that cause problems in LAM and TSC patients. The study also seeks to learn more about how simvastatin works, when given to patients being treated with everolimus or sirolimus, and to evaluate the safety and any potential benefit to patients taking this 2-drug combi

papers.title: Open-label Study of Adjunctive GNX Treatment in Children and Adults With TSC-related Epilepsy
papers.summary: This is a Phase 3, global, open-label extension (OLE) study of adjunctive GNX treatment in children and adults with TSC who previously participated in either Study 1042-TSC-3001 or Study 1042-TSC-2001

papers.title: Long-term Trial of Topical Sirolimus to Angiofibroma in Patient With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
papers.summary: The purpose of this trial is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of long-term treatment with NPC-12G gel (0.2% sirolimus gel) to angiofibroma and other skin lesions in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex in the open-label trial.

papers.title: KidneYou - Innovative Digital Therapy
papers.summary: The aim of the study is to assess the improvement of health in patients affected by CKD when they are exposed to non-pharmacological treatment strategies as nutritional program (NP), physical activity program (PA) and mindfulness program (MP), when they are conveyed to the patient by means of digital technologies or not. In the present study, non-pharmacological interventions conveyed by a digital technology (investigational arm) will be compared to a standard, paper-based approach (control arm).

papers.title: Assessment of Adjunctive Cannabidiol Oral Solution (GWP42003-P) in Children With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC), Dravet Syndrome (DS), or Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome (LGS) Who Experience Inadequately-controlled Seizures
papers.summary: This study will be conducted to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), and efficacy of adjunctive GWP42003-P in participants \< 2 years of age with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC), Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS), or Dravet syndrome (DS).

papers.title: Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of SVG103 (Paxalisib) in Focal Cortical Dysplasia Type II (FCD-II), Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) or Hemimegalencephaly (HME)
papers.summary: This is a multinational, open-label, single-arm trial of adjunctive SVG103 (paxalisib) treatment in adults with FCD-II, TSC, and HME.

papers.title: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex: Facial Angiofibroma Skin Cream
papers.summary: The objective of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a 0.1% formulation of rapamune cream in children with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC), ages 3 years and older, who have facial angiofibromas that would benefit from treatment.

papers.title: An Open-label Extension Trial of Cannabidiol (GWP42003-P, CBD) for Seizures in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (GWPCARE6)
papers.summary: This trial consists of 2 parts: a double-blinded phase and an open-label extension phase. The open-label extension phase only will be described in this record. All participants will receive the same dose of GWP42003-P. However, investigators may subsequently decrease or increase the participant's dose until the optimal dose is found.

papers.title: Astroscape: A Study of Radiprodil on Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Effect on Seizures and Behavioral Symptoms in Patients With TSC or FCD Type II
papers.summary: Study RAD-GRIN-201 is a phase 1B/2A trial to assess safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and potential efficacy of radiprodil in participants with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) or Focal Cortical Dysplasia (FCD) type II. The study is open-label, so all participants will be treated with radiprodil. Subjects' participation in the study is expected to last up to six months in Part A and one year in Part B/long-term treatment period. The treatment period in Part B may be extended based on a favorable benefit/risk profile.

papers.title: A Study to Investigate Behavioral and Other Co-Occurring Outcomes With Epidiolex as Add-On Therapy in Participants Aged 1 to 65 Years of Age With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate behavioral and other co-occurring outcomes with EPID(I/Y)OLEX as an add-on therapy in participants aged 1 to 65 years with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) who experience seizures.

papers.title: Adjunctive Ganaxolone Treatment (Part A) in TSC Followed by Long-term Treatment (Part B)
papers.summary: To assess preliminary safety and efficacy of ganaxolone as adjunctive therapy for the treatment of primary seizure types in patients with genetically- or clinically-confirmed TSC-related epilepsy through the end of the 12 week treatment period.

papers.title: Assessment of the Pharmacokinetics of Circadin® in Children With Neurodevelopmental Disorders and Sleep Disturbances
papers.summary: There is increasing evidence that chronic sleep disorders in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), Angelman Syndrome (AS) and Smith-Magenis syndrome (SMS) are associated with disturbed melatonin secretion and melatonin administration has been shown to be effective in these populations. For children who have difficulties swallowing a tablet, Neurim has developed an age-appropriate Melatonin formulation in the form of mini-tablets which have the same dissolution profile as the Circadin® tablets product, thus should produce the same melatonin concentration-time profile with the same effec

papers.title: A Study of Everolimus in the Treatment of Neurocognitive Problems in Tuberous Sclerosis
papers.summary:
This is a single centre, two-arm, individually randomised, Phase II, double- blind, placebo-controlled trial of RAD001 (Everolimus) versus placebo in the treatment of neurocognitive problems in patients with tuberous sclerosis (TSC). The IMP is a licensed medicine in this patient group but for a different target of effect. The current trial is a proof of principle study for memory and executive function outcomes.

Following an eligibility visit, patients will be scheduled for baseline visit and randomization. They will then be followed up for 6 months undergoing both safety and neurocognitive

papers.title: Use of a Tonometer to Identify Epileptogenic Lesions During Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery
papers.summary:
Refractory epilepsy, meaning epilepsy that no longer responds to medication, is a common neurosurgical indication in children. In such cases, surgery is the treatment of choice. Complete resection of affected brain tissue is associated with highest probability of seizure freedom. However, epileptogenic brain tissue is visually identical to normal brain tissue, complicating complete resection. Modern investigative methods are of limited use.

An important subjective assessment during surgery is that affected brain tissue feels stiffer, however there is presently no way to determine this without

papers.title: Treatment With Full-spectrum Cannabis Extract of Refractory Epilepsy Associated With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC)
papers.summary: 1\. To assess treatment efficacy with YCJ-01 by changes in the number of epileptic seizures in patients with refractory epilepsy secondary to Tuberous Sclerosis Complex. 2. To assess the safety of the treatment with YCJ-01 in patients with refractory epilepsy secondary to Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.

papers.title: Assessment of Potential for Chronic Liver Injury in Participants Treated With Epidiolex (Cannabidiol) Oral Solution
papers.summary: This study will monitor for potential chronic liver injury and liver fibrosis, in participants treated with cannabidiol oral solution.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Rapamycin Versus Vigabatrin in the Prevention of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Symptoms in Infants
papers.summary: The purpose of the study is to evaluate the efficacy, tolerability, and safety of vigabatrin versus rapamycin as a preventive treatment in infants with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC).

papers.title: Stopping TSC Onset and Progression 2: Epilepsy Prevention in TSC Infants
papers.summary: This phase I/II clinical trial is an open-label clinical trial design to verify safety and dosing for TAVT-18 (sirolimus) powder for oral solution in TSC infants (N=5).

papers.title: Adjunctive GNX Treatment Compared With Placebo in Children and Adults With TSC-related Epilepsy
papers.summary: This is a Phase 3, global, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study of adjunctive GNX treatment in children and adults with TSC-related epilepsy. The study consists of a 4-week prospective Baseline phase, defined as the first 28 days following screening, followed by a double-blind phase consisting of a 4-week titration period (Day 1 to Day 28) and a 12-week maintenance period (Day 29 to Week 16).

papers.title: Topical Rapamycin and Calcitriol for Angiofibroma of Tuberous Sclerosis
papers.summary:
The aim of the study is to determine the effect and safety of topical rapamycin or calcitriol and their combination for the treatment of TSC-associated facial angiofibroma.

Methods: A total of 52 TSC patients including 20 male and 32 female subjects were recruited, and 50 of them completed the period 1 study. In period 1, topical rapamycin (0.1%) or calcitriol (3 mcg/g) single-agent therapy versus their combination were applied twice a day by a left-right randomized, split-face comparison for 12 weeks. The primary end point was the reduction of facial angiofibroma severity index (FASI) for th

papers.title: Topical Rapamycin Therapy to Alleviate Cutaneous Manifestations of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) and Neurofibromatosis I (NF1)
papers.summary:
This study is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled evaluation of the safety of a topically applied formulation of rapamycin to cutaneous fibromatous lesions in subjects with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) and Neurofibromatosis I (NF1). Subjects will apply either a Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) coating (Skincerity) containing rapamycin or the PVDF coating alone nightly to fibromatous lesions for a duration of six months.

The primary goal of this study is to evaluate the safety of the topical product in patients with TSC and NF1. The secondary goal of this study is to

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Circadin® in the Treatment of Sleep Disturbances in Children With Neurodevelopment Disabilities
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to establish the efficacy and safety of Circadin in children with neurodevelopmental disorders and to determine the dose, this randomized, placebo-controlled study is planned to evaluate the efficacy of a double-blind, 13 week treatment period with Circadin 2/5mg in improving maintenance of sleep, sleep latency and additional parameters in children with neurodevelopmental disabilities. The efficacy and safety of Circadin 2/5 mg will continue to be assessed during an open-label extension period of 13 weeks.

papers.title: A Smart Phone Application to Improve Adoption of the 2024 Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) Guidelines
papers.summary:
The goal of this study is to establish whether use of a digital intervention can improve adherence and alignment with the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) 2024 Guidelines.

A subset of the study will focus on whether the intervention improves outcomes for young adults living with CKD, in the context of the imminent co-location of Children's Health Ireland on the St. James's Hospital campus.

Young adults with CKD transitioning to adult services are recognised as a high-risk and vulnerable cohort, with many individuals unaware of increased cardiovas

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of AV078 in Participants With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) Refractory Epilepsy (RESTOR-1)
papers.summary:
This Phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study will evaluate the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of oral AV078 in participants with refractory epilepsy due to tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC). Approximately 42 participants will be randomized in a 5:1 ratio to receive AV078 or placebo.

The study will include a Screening Period collecting 4 weeks of pre-treatment Baseline data on seizure frequency, and progress to a 12-week Treatment Period, followed by an in person final follow-up visit approximately 2 weeks after the last dose.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Everolimus (RAD001) in Patients of All Ages With Subependymal Giant Cell Astrocytoma Associated With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC)(EXIST-1)
papers.summary: This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of Everolimus in treating patients with Subependymal Giant Cell Astrocytomas associated with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.

papers.title: Sapu003 in Advanced mTOR-sensitive Solid Tumors
papers.summary: This is a phase 1b, open-label, dose-escalation study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics of Sapu003 in combination with Exemestane in in patients with advanced mTOR-sensitive solid tumors (HR+/HER2-negative breast cancer, renal cell carcinoma \[RCC\], neuroendocrine tumors \[NETs\], tuberous sclerosis complex \[TSC\]-associated tumors, and hepatocellular carcinoma \[HCC\]).

papers.title: Topical Everolimus in Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
papers.summary: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a rare genetic multisystem disorder characterized by the development of hamartomas in several organs (e.g. brain, heart, kidney, liver, lung), and skin in more than 90% of cases. Facial angiofibromas (FA), present in about 80% of patients, are a stigmatizing hallmark of the disease. Everolimus could be a candidate for use as a topical formulation to treat FA. This adaptive seamless Phase II/III study primary objective is to determine the dose of topical everolimus for treatment of FA and evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical everolimus versus placebo i

papers.title: Everolimus for Cancer With TSC1 or TSC2 Mutation
papers.summary:
In this research study, the investigators are evaluating the clinical benefit of everolimus in cancer patients with inactivating TSC1 or TSC2 mutations or activating MTOR mutations.

This research study is a Phase II clinical trial, which tests the safety and effectiveness of an investigational drug called everolimus to learn whether the drug works in treating a specific cancer. "Investigational" means that the drug is being studied. It also means that the FDA (the U.S. Food and Drug Administration) has not yet approved everolimus for your type of cancer.
