papers.title: A Phase II Study of Orally Administered BEZ235 Monotherapy in Patients With Metastatic or Unresectable Malignant PEComa
papers.summary:
Study objectives:

The primary objective is to determine the efficacy of BEZ235 on Objective Response Rate (best response on study) according to RECIST 1.1 criteria

The secondary objectives are:

* To determine the progression free survival rate at 32 weeks in the included population
* To assess the duration of response among responders
* To evaluate time to response
* To evaluate the time to progression
* To assess the overall survival
* To evaluate safety and tolerability of BEZ235

The exploratory objectives are:

* To identify molecular and genomic profiles of PEComas and their potential

papers.title: Rapalogues for Autism Phenotype in TSC: A Feasibility Study
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to assess the feasibility and safety of administering rapalogues, sirolimus or everolimus, in participants with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) and self-injury and to measure cognitive and behavioral changes, including reduction in autistic symptoms, self-injurious and aggressive behaviors, as well as improvements in cognition across multiple domains of cognitive function.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of Everolimus (Afinitor®) in Chinese Adult Patients With Angiomyolipoma Associated With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
papers.summary: The purpose of this study was to assess the safety and efficacy of everolimus (Afinitor®) in Chinese patients with renal angiomyolipoma (AML) associated with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC).

papers.title: Basimglurant (NOE-101) in Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults With TSC
papers.summary: The study intends to show that basimglurant (NOE-101) provides effective seizure control in children, adolescents and young adults with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC).

papers.title: Study to Evaluate the Pharmacokinetics and Safety Effects Following Coadministration of Carbamazepine or Itraconazole With Radiprodil in Healthy Adults
papers.summary: This is a Phase 1, open-label, 2-part study to evaluate the effect of multiple doses of oral carbamazepine or oral itraconazole on the plasma pharmacokinetic profile of radiprodil in healthy adult participants. In addition, the safety and tolerability of radiprodil given together with oral carbamazepine or itraconazole will be assessed.

papers.title: Stopping TSC Onset and Progression 2B: Sirolimus TSC Epilepsy Prevention Study
papers.summary:
This trial is a Phase II randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled multi-site study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of early sirolimus to prevent or delay seizure onset in TSC infants.

This study is supported by research funding from the Office of Orphan Products Division (OOPD) of the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

papers.title: Dose-Ranging Efficacy and Safety Study of Topical Rapamycin Cream for Facial Angiofibroma Associated With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
papers.summary: The study aims to compare the safety and efficacy of two different strengths of Rapamycin cream, topical and placebo over 26 weeks in the treatment of facial angiofibroma (FA) associated with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC).

papers.title: A Pilot Study To Evaluate The Effects of Everolimus on Brain mTOR Activity and Cortical Hyperexcitability in TSC and FCD
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to measure if the drug called Everolimus effects mTOR signaling (an electrical activity signal in the brain) in patients with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) and Focal Cortical Dysplasia (FCD) with treatment resistant epilepsy (TRE) who will be undergoing brain surgery. One group of patients will be treated with Everolimus, and another will not. Researchers will determine if there is a difference in mTOR signaling between the patients who were treated with Everolimus and those who were not. Previous studies have suggested that Everolimus may reduce seizure activit

papers.title: A Phase IV Study of Safety and Efficacy of Everolimus in Taiwanese Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Who Have Renal Angiomyolipoma (TSC-AML)
papers.summary: The purpose of this prospective study is to assess the safety and efficacy of everolimus in Taiwanese patients with renal angiomyolipoma (AML) associated with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) . Only patients who fulfil the local reimbursement criteria of everolimus for TSC-AML will be included in this study.

papers.title: Phase III Trial of Topical Formulation of Sirolimus to Skin Lesions in Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC)
papers.summary: The purpose of this trial is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of NPC-12G gel (topical formulation of sirolimus) versus placebo gel to facial angiofibroma and other skin lesions in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC)

papers.title: Efficacy of RAD001/Everolimus in Autism and NeuroPsychological Deficits in Children With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
papers.summary: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a genetic disease that leads to mental retardation in over 50% of patients, and to learning problems, behavioral problems, autism and epilepsy in up to 90% of patients. The underlying deficit of TSC, loss of inhibition of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) protein due to dysfunction of the tuberin/hamartin protein complex, can be rescued by everolimus. Everolimus has been registered as treatment for renal cell carcinoma and giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA). Evidence in human and animal studies suggests that mTOR inhibitors improve learning and development

papers.title: Sertraline vs. Placebo in the Treatment of Anxiety in Children and AdoLescents With NeurodevelopMental Disorders
papers.summary: There are currently no approved medications for the treatment of anxiety in children and youth with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), both common and rare. Sertraline, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, has extensive evidence to support its use in children's and youth with anxiety but not within NDDs. More research is needed to confirm whether or not sertraline could help improve anxiety in children and youth with common and rare neurodevelopmental conditions. This is a pilot study, in which we plan to estimate the effect size of reduction in anxiety of sertraline vs. placebo. across

papers.title: Turmeric as Treatment in Epilepsy
papers.summary: This is a single center open-label pilot clinical trial of patients 1-70 years of age with greater than 6 seizures per month diagnosed with Dravet Syndrome, Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome, Tuberous Sclerosis, or focal seizures. Twenty patients will be enrolled and treated with a stable dose of orally administered turmeric oil daily for 3 months. Patients and caregivers will be asked to keep a seizure diary logging all clinical events during the course of the study. Serum comprehensive metabolic panel, complete blood count with differential, and antiseizure medication levels, will be monitored at base

papers.title: Preventing Epilepsy Using Vigabatrin In Infants With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
papers.summary: Study design is a Phase IIb prospective multi-center, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial. The goal will be to enroll 80 infants with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex who are less than 6 months of age prior to the onset of their first seizure

papers.title: RAD001 Therapy of Angiomyolipomata in Patients With TS Complex and Sporadic LAM
papers.summary:
The purpose of this research study is to find out what effects RAD001 has on angiomyolipomas of a person with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex and to determine the safe dose of RAD001 without toxicity.

The hypothesis is that the drug will inhibit the growth of the angiomyolipomas and possibly even cause regression.

papers.title: Characterizing Sleep Disorders in Children and Adults With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC)
papers.summary: The proposed research project is aimed at further characterization of sleep problems and evaluation of their impact in children and adults with TSC, excluding epilepsy as contributing factor. Questionnaire-based studies have shown that sleep problems occur in up to half of the children and a third of adults with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC). However, there is only limited information on the nature of sleep problems and their impact on patients with TSC and their families.

papers.title: Topical Rapamycin to Erase Angiofibromas in TSC
papers.summary:
The study is a multi-center prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled evaluation of the safety and efficacy of a topically applied formulation of rapamycin to cutaneous angiofibromas in subjects with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC). Subjects will apply either the topical vehicle containing rapamycin or the topical vehicle alone nightly to their angiofibromas for six months.

The primary goal of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of the topical medication for reduction of cutaneous angiofibromas in patients with TSC. The secondary goal of this study is to confirm the safety

papers.title: A Placebo-controlled Study of Efficacy & Safety of 2 Trough-ranges of Everolimus as Adjunctive Therapy in Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) & Refractory Partial-onset Seizures
papers.summary:
This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of two trough-ranges of everolimus given as adjunctive therapy in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) who had refractory partial-onset seizures.

The study consisted of 4 phases for each patient Baseline phase:\[From Screening Week -8 (V1) to randomization visit at Week 0 (V2)\], Core phase \[from randomization at Week 0 (V2) to Week 18 (V11)\], Extension phase \[from Week 18 (V11) until 48 weeks after the last patient had completed the core phase\] and Post Extension phase \[from end of Extension phase to end of study\].

papers.title: Rapamycin In Angiomyolipomas In Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine whether rapamycin is safe and effective in the treatment of renal angiomyolipomas in patients with tuberousclerosis.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for tuberous sclerosis
Open Targets drugs acting on GRM5
Modeling mTORopathy-related epilepsy in cultured murine hippocampal neurons using the multi-electrode array.
papers.summary: Cultured mouse hippocampal neurons with Tsc1 deletion or constitutively active RHEB p.P37L produced mTORC1-hyperactive, epilepsy-like network phenotypes measurable by multi-electrode arrays. Early rapamycin treatment prevented these phenotypes, whereas treatment of mature cultures partially rescued them; vigabatrin reduced network activity and restored burst characteristics.

papers.title: Enhanced Gαq Signaling in <i>TSC2</i>-Deficient Cells Is Required for Their Neoplastic Behavior.
papers.journal: Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol
papers.summary: This paper identifies an mTORC1-independent mechanism of neoplastic behavior in TSC2-deficient pulmonary lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) cells: hyperactivation of urotensin-II receptor (UT) signaling through heterotrimeric Gαq/11 and increased endosomal targeting of p63RhoGEF. In vitro findings suggest that targeting this UT–Gαq–RhoA pathway could prevent or eradicate pulmonary and extrapulmonary LAM tumors, although rapamycin slows but does not eradicate LAM.

papers.title: STAT3 regulates the generation of astroglia in human brain organoids with high mTORC1 activity
papers.summary: In human brain organoids, high mTORC1 signaling resulting from TSC2 deletion promotes glial-lineage production through STAT3. STAT3 knockdown reduces astrogliogenesis, although mTORC1 signaling is not required for cytokine-induced STAT3 activation or GFAP expression.

papers.title: Inhibition of mTORC1 Signaling Reverts Cognitive and Affective Deficits in a Mouse Model of Parkinson's Disease.
papers.summary: In a partial bilateral 6-hydroxydopamine mouse model of Parkinson’s disease, rapamycin reduced the cognitive, depression-like, and anxiety-like deficits associated with mTORC1 inhibition and rescued novel object recognition, whereas selective S6K inhibition rescued memory but did not substantially rescue affective behavior. The paper also identifies excessive mTORC1 activation and rapamycin-sensitive cognitive impairment in tuberous sclerosis as a review-level mechanistic link supporting transfer of mTORC1-directed strategies.

papers.title: Exosomal miR-4645-5p from hypoxic bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells facilitates diabetic wound healing by restoring keratinocyte autophagy.
papers.summary: Hypoxic bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes transferred miR-4645-5p to keratinocytes, where it inhibited MAPKAPK2 and thereby reduced AKT-mTORC1 signaling, restoring autophagy and promoting proliferation, migration, and diabetic wound healing. The mechanism was supported in human HaCaT keratinocytes and full-thickness wounds in db/db mice, with miR-4645-5p knockdown attenuating these effects.

papers.title: Microglial AKAP8L: a key mediator in diabetes-associated cognitive impairment via autophagy inhibition and neuroinflammation triggering.
papers.summary: In high-glucose-treated microglia and STZ-induced diabetic mice, AKAP8L accumulated and interacted with mTORC1 while autophagy was impaired and neuroinflammation increased. AKAP8L knockdown and rapamycin suppressed mTORC1 signaling, restored autophagic measures, reduced inflammation and pyroptosis, and improved cognitive and hippocampal neuronal outcomes, although rapamycin is noted to have adverse effects associated with mTORC2 inhibition.

papers.title: RXR Gamma Enables Oligodendrocyte Differentiation by Suppressing Sonic Hedgehog Signaling.
papers.summary: In mouse Rxrg−/− oligodendrocyte precursor-cell models, loss of retinoid X receptor gamma (RXRg) elevates sonic hedgehog signaling, blocks triiodothyronine-induced oligodendrocyte differentiation and maturation, and impairs myelination. Cyclopamine and GANT61 normalize these defects in knockout cells, whereas SAG and purmorphamine induce differentiation blocks in wild-type cells, indicating that tightly controlled SHH signaling is required for oligodendrocyte development.

papers.title: Selective GPR17 antagonism enhances structural and functional recovery in animal models of demyelination.
papers.summary: Selective GPR17 antagonism with the oral small molecule RWT020016 promoted structural and functional recovery in acute and chronic cuprizone mouse models of demyelination, with effects consistent with release of an oligodendrocyte precursor-cell differentiation block. Human multiple-sclerosis tissue showed GPR17 enrichment in committed oligodendrocyte precursor cells near demyelinated lesions, supporting transfer of this oligodendrocyte-directed remyelination strategy to disorders with comparable myelin-repair failure, but efficacy in tuberous sclerosis was not tested.

papers.title: Honokiol attenuates neuroinflammation and enhances remyelination in mouse models of multiple sclerosis through PPARγ-mediated ERK/AKT signalling.
papers.summary: In two mouse models of multiple sclerosis, honokiol reduced inflammatory demyelination and increased remyelination, while directly promoting differentiation of oligodendrocyte precursor cells into mature oligodendrocytes in vitro. Pharmacological blockade identified PPARγ-dependent ERK/AKT activation, rather than CB1, CB2, or mTOR activation, as the principal mechanism supporting oligodendrocyte maturation.

papers.title: Growth Differentiation Factor 11 Is a Circulating Regulator of Oligodendrocyte Differentiation and CNS Myelin Formation and Repair.
papers.summary: Systemically administered GDF11 promoted oligodendrocyte progenitor cell differentiation, accelerated developmental myelination, and improved remyelination and functional recovery in cuprizone and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis mouse models. It did not prevent active cuprizone-induced demyelination, and its enhancement of developmental myelination was transient, supporting GDF11 as a candidate oligodendrocyte-directed myelin-repair therapy.

papers.title: Maternal microbiome-derived propionate regulates offspring myelination via histone lactylation.
papers.summary: Maternal antibiotic-induced gut dysbiosis caused hypomyelination in offspring, and postnatal propionate supplementation rescued this phenotype. Propionate also promoted oligodendrocyte precursor cell differentiation and remyelination through induction of H4K12 lactylation and activation of cGMP-PKG signaling, including the pathway component Gna12.

papers.title: Remodeling oligodendrocyte lipid metabolism via liver X receptors overcomes inflammatory blockade of remyelination
papers.summary: The paper shows that inflammation in multiple sclerosis reprograms oligodendrocyte precursor lipid metabolism from synthesis toward oxidation, reducing intracellular fatty acids and impairing precursor differentiation into myelinating oligodendrocytes. Enhancing lipid availability or activating liver X receptors restored differentiation-related functions in cultured cells and increased mature oligodendrocyte generation and myelin repair in an inflammatory demyelination mouse model.

papers.title: Effect of the mGluR5-NAM Basimglurant on Behavior in Adolescents and Adults with Fragile X Syndrome in a Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial: FragXis Phase 2 Results.
papers.summary: The FragXis phase 2 trial found that basimglurant, a selective negative allosteric modulator of the GRM5/mGluR5 mechanism, did not improve behavioral or functional outcomes in adolescents and adults with Fragile X syndrome compared with placebo. Psychiatric adverse events, including hallucinations or psychosis, were more frequent with basimglurant, and exploratory FMR1 methylation, mRNA, and FMRP biomarkers did not predict treatment response.

papers.title: Contribution of mGluR5 to pathophysiology in a mouse model of human chromosome 16p11.2 microdeletion.
papers.summary: The study shows that hippocampal mGluR5-dependent synaptic plasticity and protein-synthesis regulation are altered in 16p11.2 df/+ mice, accompanied by impaired contextual fear conditioning and inhibitory-avoidance memory. Chronic treatment with the mGluR5 negative allosteric modulator CTEP corrected the mutant mice’s inhibitory-avoidance acquisition and extinction deficits, supporting a transferable approach for diseases involving GRM5-dependent glutamatergic plasticity.

papers.title: The eIF2α kinase PERK limits the expression of hippocampal metabotropic glutamate receptor-dependent long-term depression.
papers.summary: The study shows that PERK-dependent phosphorylation of eukaryotic initiation factor 2 alpha (eIF2α) normally limits group I metabotropic glutamate receptor-dependent long-term depression (mGluR-LTD) in mouse hippocampal CA1 neurons. Forebrain-specific PERK deletion enhanced mGluR-LTD without altering mGluR5 expression, early- or late-phase LTP, basal transmission, or paired-pulse facilitation; anisomycin blocked the enhanced LTD, indicating dependence on new protein synthesis.

papers.title: Inhibition of the ISR abrogates mGluR5-dependent long-term depression and spatial memory deficits in a rat model of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: In adult male Wistar rats injected intracerebroventricularly with soluble amyloid-β1–42, the selective GRM5/mGluR5 antagonist MTEP blocked facilitated hippocampal long-term depression, demonstrating a GRM5-dependent synaptic mechanism. The integrated stress response inhibitor ISRIB also prevented the long-term depression and spatial learning and memory deficits while restoring hippocampal protein synthesis, but its protection was not shown to require direct GRM5 modulation.

papers.title: Is metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 upregulated in prefrontal cortex in fragile X syndrome?
papers.summary: In postmortem prefrontal cortex from individuals with fragile X syndrome or premutation carriers, GRM5 receptor density was marginally higher and GRM5 protein expression was significantly higher than in matched controls. The paper also summarizes evidence that GRM5 negative allosteric modulators can improve behavioral or cognitive features in fragile X syndrome models and patients, while highlighting mixed human trial efficacy and major confounders.

papers.title: Sarm1 deficiency impairs synaptic function and leads to behavioral deficits, which can be ameliorated by an mGluR allosteric modulator.
papers.summary: In Sarm1-knockdown mice and Sarm1-shRNA-transfected hippocampal neurons, the paper shows impaired mGluR5/GRM5-dependent long-term depression, enhanced NMDAR-dependent long-term potentiation, and autistic-like behavioral deficits. The GRM5 positive allosteric modulator CDPPB rescued the electrophysiological LTD defect and improved contextual fear conditioning and reciprocal social interaction, while the paper also cites evidence that TSC2+/- tuberous sclerosis models share abnormal mGluR signaling.

papers.title: Myeloid cells expressing VEGF and arginase-1 following uptake of damaged retinal pigment epithelium suggests potential mechanism that drives the onset of choroidal angiogenesis in mice.
papers.summary: The study shows that laser-induced retinal pigment epithelium/Bruch’s membrane injury recruits CCR2-positive blood monocytes before choroidal angiogenesis, and that these cells acquire an ARG1-positive, VEGF-positive phenotype after taking up damaged retinal pigment epithelium. Depletion of CCR2-positive monocytes with the MC-21 antibody reduced lesional ARG1 and VEGF signals and suppressed neovascular complex volume by 39%, identifying the CCL2–CCR2-dependent monocyte recruitment axis as a potential intervention point.

papers.title: Activin promotes skin carcinogenesis by attraction and reprogramming of macrophages.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of HPV8-induced skin carcinogenesis, activin A promoted monocyte recruitment to skin and reprogrammed the recruited cells toward a tumor-associated macrophage phenotype. Depletion of CCR2-positive monocytes reduced keratinocyte proliferation, while macrophage depletion with anti-CSF1R antibody delayed tumor formation, supporting monocyte recruitment and macrophages as mechanistically relevant intervention points.

papers.title: Targeting cardiac resident CCR2+ macrophage-secreted MCP-1 to attenuate inflammation after myocardial infarction.
papers.summary: The paper shows that targeted delivery of the MCP-1-binding HSW peptide in platelet-membrane-cloaked nanoparticles reduces monocyte recruitment, pro-inflammatory macrophage accumulation, inflammation, and fibrosis after acute myocardial infarction in mice. HSW also directly inhibited MCP-1-induced monocyte migration, inflammatory cytokine expression, and cardiac fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation in vitro, although selected effects such as early fibrosis reduction and angiogenesis were null.

papers.title: Pharmacological inhibition of the CCL2-CCR2 axis fails to reduce inflammation in a rat model of acute lung injury.
papers.summary: In a rat HCl/LPS-induced acute lung injury model, a single intratracheal dose of a CCL2-neutralizing antibody or CCR2 antagonist transiently reduced monocyte recruitment into the bronchoalveolar space at 24 h, but did not sustain this effect or significantly improve inflammation, lung damage, or function at 72 h. The results indicate that late, single-dose inhibition of the CCL2-CCR2 axis is insufficient to control monocyte-driven acute lung injury.

papers.title: CCL2-CCR2 Axis Inhibition in Osteosarcoma Cell Model: The Impact of Oxygen Level on Cell Phenotype.
papers.summary: The study shows that inhibiting the CCL2-CCR2 axis with the CCR2 antagonist RS504393 alters monocyte/macrophage infiltration and tumor-cell phenotypes in a 143B osteosarcoma model, but it does not reduce tumor growth or pulmonary metastatic burden. Hypoxia substantially changes the molecular response to CCR2 inhibition, suggesting that compensatory angiogenesis, cell-adhesion, hypoxia, and drug-resistance programs may limit transfer of this intervention to mechanisms involving monocyte recruitment.

papers.title: CCL2 Inhibitor Bindarit Improve Postoperative Cognitive Function by Attenuating Pericyte Loss-Related Blood-Brain Barrier Disruption and Neuroinflammation.
papers.summary: In an aged-mouse tibial-surgery model of perioperative neurocognitive disorder, the CCL2 inhibitor Bindarit reduced hippocampal CCL2 overexpression, preserved pericyte and capillary coverage, maintained blood–brain barrier integrity, and improved cognitive and anxiety-related outcomes. The paper identifies CCL2 as a chemokine that recruits monocytes/macrophages through CCR2, making the Bindarit–CCL2 intervention mechanistically relevant to monocyte recruitment.

unread.title: Genotype and brain pathology phenotype in children with tuberous sclerosis complex.
unread.why: The study validates MRI-based brain-pathology measures and shows that TSC1 versus TSC2 genotype can stratify cortical tubers, radial migration lines, and subependymal nodule severity in children with TSC.

unread.title: Mutational analysis of TSC1 and TSC2 in Japanese patients with tuberous sclerosis complex revealed higher incidence of TSC1 patients than previously reported.
unread.why: Mutational testing of 57 Japanese patients provides a disease-specific diagnostic assay and evidence that TSC1 and TSC2 genotypes differ in developmental severity.

unread.title: Functional assessment of variants in the TSC1 and TSC2 genes identified in individuals with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
unread.why: A standardized laboratory protocol functionally assessed 152 TSC1/TSC2 variants and classified variants as pathogenic or probably neutral, directly supporting variant interpretation and diagnosis.

unread.title: Missense mutations to the TSC1 gene cause tuberous sclerosis complex.
unread.why: The study experimentally links specific TSC1 substitutions to reduced protein abundance, altered TSC1–TSC2 complex formation, and mTOR activation.

unread.title: Novel TSC1 and TSC2 gene mutations in Chinese patients with tuberous sclerosis complex.
unread.why: PCR amplification and variant identification confirmed the molecular diagnosis in 11 patients and expanded the catalog of pathogenic TSC1/TSC2 variants.

unread.title: Identification of the tuberous sclerosis gene TSC1 on chromosome 9q34.
unread.why: Identification of TSC1 and characterization of 32 disease-associated mutations established a causal gene and a concrete variant-testing resource for TSC.

unread.title: Mutational analysis in a cohort of 224 tuberous sclerosis patients indicates increased severity of TSC2, compared with TSC1, disease in multiple organs.
unread.why: The cohort provides a molecular testing workflow and a standardized clinical instrument for assessing 16 manifestations and relating TSC genotype to multisystem severity.

unread.title: Genotype/phenotype correlation in 325 individuals referred for a diagnosis of tuberous sclerosis complex in the United States.
unread.why: Large-cohort molecular analysis and meta-analysis identify genotype-associated patterns across neurological, renal, ocular, dermatologic, and learning phenotypes that can support prognosis and management.

unread.title: Central TSC2 missense mutations are associated with a reduced risk of infantile spasms.
unread.why: Analysis of 478 patients shows that centrally located TSC2 missense variants identify a subgroup with reduced infantile-spasm risk, providing a genotype-based prognostic biomarker.

unread.title: Topical Use of Mammalian Target of Rapamycin (mTOR) Inhibitors in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex-A Comprehensive Review of the Literature.
unread.why: Reviews clinical evidence that topical mTOR inhibitors treat TSC-associated cutaneous lesions, particularly facial angiofibromas.

unread.title: Mutational analysis of TSC1 and TSC2 in Danish patients with tuberous sclerosis complex.
unread.why: Provides a large TSC patient cohort, mutation-detection methods, and functional testing for resolving uncertain TSC2 variants.

unread.title: Epilepsy Risk Prediction Model for Patients With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
unread.why: Develops and validates a clinical model using sex, genotype and tuber presence to predict epilepsy risk in TSC.

unread.title: Advances in the genetics and neuropathology of tuberous sclerosis complex: edging closer to targeted therapy.
unread.why: Reviews established and emerging TSC interventions, including mTOR inhibitors, vigabatrin, and EEG/MRI risk stratification.

unread.title: Applying the Lessons of Tuberous Sclerosis: The 2015 Hower Award Lecture.
unread.why: Synthesizes mechanism-based clinical evidence for mTOR inhibition in TSC tumors and refractory epilepsy.

unread.title: The phosphoproteomic landscape of the neurological manifestations in tuberous sclerosis complex.
unread.why: Provides human TSC tuber and SEGA molecular profiling data that identify pathway alterations, biomarkers and disease mechanisms.

unread.title: Multisystem Imaging Features of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex: The First Case Series from Somalia with a Comprehensive Literature Review
unread.why: Demonstrates that characteristic MRI and ultrasound findings can establish TSC diagnosis and support multisystem surveillance when genetic testing is unavailable.

unread.title: Precision Treatment of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex: A Case Report of Sirolimus Toxicity in a CYP3A5 Poor Metabolizer Neonate and Pharmacogenomic Literature Review
unread.why: Reports pharmacogenomic-guided sirolimus dosing that corrected toxic exposure in a neonate with TSC and reviews a transferable precision-dosing framework.

unread.title: The phosphoproteomic landscape of the neurological manifestations in tuberous sclerosis complex
unread.why: Presents an experimental phosphoproteomic resource and method for identifying molecular alterations and potential biomarkers in TSC neurological lesions.

unread.title: Late diagnosis and effective everolimus treatment in a familial case of tuberous sclerosis complex: a case report.
unread.why: A familial TSC case with seizure and angiofibroma improvement after everolimus provides direct clinical evidence while highlighting molecular confirmation of diagnosis.

unread.title: Late-Onset Diagnosis of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Revealed by Renal Angiomyolipoma: A Case Report.
unread.why: This late-onset TSC case demonstrates sirolimus for residual renal angiomyolipomas, surgical treatment, and an applicable diagnostic and surveillance strategy.

unread.title: Tuberous sclerosis complex consensus conference: revised clinical diagnostic criteria.
unread.why: The paper establishes validated diagnostic criteria for TSC and clarifies how to interpret clinical, radiographic, and family-history findings.

unread.title: Mutational analysis of the TSC1 and TSC2 genes in a diagnostic setting: genotype--phenotype correlations and comparison of diagnostic DNA techniques in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
unread.why: A 490-patient study validates a multi-technique TSC1/TSC2 diagnostic workflow and reports its mutation-detection performance and phenotype correlations.

unread.title: Comprehensive mutation analysis of TSC1 and TSC2-and phenotypic correlations in 150 families with tuberous sclerosis.
unread.why: The study provides a validated comprehensive genetic testing workflow with an 80% detection rate and data linking TSC1 versus TSC2 genotypes to severity.

unread.title: Functional characterization of the TSC2 c.3598C>T (p.R1200W) missense mutation that co-segregates with tuberous sclerosis complex in mildly affected kindreds.
unread.why: The paper experimentally characterizes a recurrent TSC2 variant and four mild-disease variants, providing a functional approach for variant interpretation.

unread.title: Paradigm shift in the treatment of tuberous sclerosis: Effectiveness of everolimus.
unread.why: The review consolidates evidence that everolimus treats TSC-associated hamartomas and manifestations across multiple organs by correcting dysregulated mTORC1 signaling.

unread.title: Comprehensive Genetic Analysis Results of TSC1/TSC2 Genes in Patients with Clinical Suspicion of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex and Definition of 3 Novel Variants.
unread.why: The study demonstrates a comprehensive diagnostic workflow that detects TSC2 variants, large rearrangements, and low-allele-fraction mosaic changes.

unread.title: Cell-cell communication dysregulation in tuberous sclerosis complex cortical tubers and focal cortical dysplasia.
unread.why: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling directly characterizes TSC cortical tubers and identifies measurable cell populations and dysregulated synaptic signaling that can guide mechanistic or therapeutic studies.

unread.title: Quick genetic screening using targeted next-generation sequencing in patients with tuberous sclerosis.
unread.why: The study validates targeted next-generation sequencing as a faster, less costly primary method for detecting TSC mutations.

unread.title: CRISPR-Cas9 Single Nucleotide Editing of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex 2 Gene in Mesenchymal Stem Cells.
unread.why: The paper establishes an efficient, reversible CRISPR workflow for introducing recurrent TSC2 point mutations directly into human mesenchymal stem cells.

unread.title: Maternal Sirolimus Treatment Reverses Cardiac Rhabdomyoma-Induced Hydrops Fetalis in a Twin Gestation With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
unread.why: A case report provides direct evidence that maternal sirolimus reversed fetal hydrops caused by a massive TSC-associated cardiac rhabdomyoma.

unread.title: Analysis of both TSC1 and TSC2 for germline mutations in 126 unrelated patients with tuberous sclerosis.
unread.why: The study provides substantial TSC patient data validating combined TSC1/TSC2 mutation screening and defining detectable pathogenic variant patterns.

unread.title: Emerging treatments in the management of tuberous sclerosis complex.
unread.why: The paper summarizes clinical-trial evidence for sirolimus and everolimus as disease-directed treatments for TSC hamartomas.

unread.title: Analysis of 65 tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) patients by TSC2 DGGE, TSC1/TSC2 MLPA, and TSC1 long-range PCR sequencing, and report of 28 novel mutations.
unread.why: The combined molecular workflow achieved a 78% diagnostic yield in 65 TSC patients and included a functional assay for missense variants.

unread.title: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Genotypes and Developmental Phenotype.
unread.why: Prospective TSC data show that the validated Mullen Scales can quantify developmental domains and identify elevated developmental-delay risk associated with TSC2 variants.

unread.title: Long-Term Everolimus Treatment in Individuals With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex: A Review of the Current Literature.
unread.why: Synthesizes clinical evidence that everolimus suppresses TSC-associated lesions and may be feasible indefinitely with limited long-term safety concerns.

unread.title: Topical everolimus for facial angiofibromas in the tuberous sclerosis complex. A first case report.
unread.why: Reports successful treatment of disfiguring facial angiofibromas with topical everolimus and no relevant side effects in a TSC patient.

unread.title: Antenatal screening and diagnosis of tuberous sclerosis complex by fetal echocardiography and targeted genomic sequencing.
unread.why: Demonstrates that fetal cardiac rhabdomyoma detected by echocardiography, combined with targeted sequencing, can support prenatal TSC screening and diagnosis.

unread.title: Hemispherectomy for Hemimegalencephaly Due to Tuberous Sclerosis and a Review of the Literature.
unread.why: Reports successful functional hemispherectomy with nearly five years of seizure freedom after surgery in an infant with TSC-related hemimegalencephaly.

unread.title: Comprehensive mutation analysis of TSC1 using two-dimensional DNA electrophoresis with DGGE.
unread.why: Develops and validates a two-dimensional DGGE genetic assay that detected all known mutations in the study and identified additional variants.

unread.title: Screening for TSC1 and TSC2 mutations using NGS in Greek children with tuberous sclerosis syndrome.
unread.why: The study validates a custom NGS diagnostic panel with an 88% mutation detection rate and creates a mutation registry for children with TSC.

unread.title: Combination of Multiple Ligation-Dependent Probe Amplification and Illumina MiSeq Amplicon Sequencing for TSC1/TSC2 Gene Analyses in Patients with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
unread.why: The combined assay detects both small TSC1/TSC2 variants and large copy-number changes with reduced cost and turnaround time, making it directly reusable for molecular diagnosis.

unread.title: Minute amounts of hamartin wildtype rescue the emergence of tuber-like lesions in conditional Tsc1 ablated mice.
unread.why: Minimal wild-type TSC1 expression rescued tuber-like neuronal lesions in a conditional mouse/electroporation model, providing a concrete gene-therapy rationale and reusable disease model.

unread.title: Translatome analysis of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex-1 patient-derived neural progenitor cells reveal rapamycin-dependent and independent alterations.
unread.why: The study provides a TSC patient-derived neural model, transcriptomic translation assay, and experimental evidence that rapamycin or RMC-6272 can reverse molecular and neurodevelopmental abnormalities.

unread.title: Epilepsy surgery for tuberous sclerosis.
unread.why: Existing surgery is reported to reduce or abolish medically intractable TSC seizures, while EEG, neuroimaging, and cortical mapping can identify candidates and resectable epileptogenic zones.

unread.title: Subependymal giant cell astrocytomas in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex: considerations for surgical or pharmacotherapeutic intervention.
unread.why: The paper identifies two existing intervention strategies for TSC-associated subependymal giant cell astrocytoma and describes criteria and risks for choosing surgery versus pathway-targeted pharmacotherapy.

unread.title: Successful Everolimus Therapy for Atrioventricular Block Due to Cardiac Rhabdomyoma Associated With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
unread.why: A TSC case provides direct evidence that everolimus regressed cardiac rhabdomyomas and resolved the associated atrioventricular block.

unread.title: Tuberous sclerosis complex.
unread.why: This review identifies approved rapalogues for multiple TSC manifestations and summarizes their established use for subependymal giant cell astrocytomas, renal angiomyolipomas, pulmonary lymphangiomyomatosis, facial angiofibromas, and refractory seizures.

unread.title: Amyloid-Independent Elevation of Plasma phosphorylated tau-217 Tracks Neurodegenerative Risk in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex: Implications for mTOR-Targeted Intervention
unread.why: Patient-cohort data show that plasma ptau-217 is elevated in TSC and support its use as a minimally invasive biomarker for neurodegenerative risk, prognosis, and stratification for mTOR-targeted strategies.

unread.title: The Activation of the Transcription Factor NRF2 in Epithelial Cells Lining the Kidney Cysts in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC): The Interplay of Fumarate Hydratase 1, KEAP1, and NRF2 in Kidney Cystogenesis
unread.why: Multi-omic and imaging experiments in TSC1-knockout kidneys identify an NRF2-centered metabolic program and show that disrupting its nutrient-supply mechanism reduces cyst burden.

unread.title: Molecular basis of TSC complex GAP activity
unread.why: The catalytic transition-state structure and functional residue analysis provide a molecular method for evaluating TSC2 and Rheb variants and identifying allosteric drug-targeting opportunities.

unread.title: The small molecule simufilam dose-dependently attenuates the worsening of seizures in a mouse model of tuberous sclerosis complex.
unread.why: Dose-dependent EEG results in a Tsc1 conditional knockout model show that simufilam attenuates seizure worsening, with accompanying pharmacokinetic characterization.

unread.title: Clinical characteristics and molecular genetic analysis of 73 cases of tuberous sclerosis complex caused by <i>TSC1/2</i> gene mutations in children.
unread.why: Whole-exome analysis of 73 pediatric cases establishes an early TSC1/TSC2 testing approach, provides genotype-phenotype outcome data, and expands the catalog of pathogenic variants for diagnosis.

unread.title: Genotype and subependymal lesion burden influence volumetric response to everolimus in tuberous sclerosis complex-associated subependymal giant cell astrocytoma: A 10-year real-world study.
unread.why: A 10-year TSC cohort provides direct evidence that everolimus reduces SEGA volume and identifies genotype and imaging measures that stratify treatment response.

unread.title: In vitro study of TSC1 deficiency in preadipocytes: insights into development and treatment options for tuberous sclerosis related lipomatosis.
unread.why: Patient-derived cellular experiments directly show that sirolimus, torin-1, and alpelisib suppress proliferation and mTOR-pathway activation in TSC1-deficient cells.

unread.title: ENT1 inhibitor J4 restores cognitive function and white-matter integrity in a mouse model of tuberous sclerosis complex.
unread.why: Treatment of a TSC2 mouse model with J4 improves cognition, anxiety-like behavior, myelination, and white-matter integrity.

unread.title: Case Report: Individualized management of tuberous sclerosis complex-associated lymphangioleiomyomatosis.
unread.why: A TSC-LAM case provides direct evidence of stable disease with individualized sirolimus and describes an integrated monitoring and family-screening approach.

unread.title: Genotype and Cardiac Rhabdomyoma Phenotype Analyses in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Diseases.
unread.why: The analysis provides a reusable genotype-phenotype resource for interpreting TSC variants associated with cardiac rhabdomyoma.

unread.title: Prenatal therapy of everolimus for large fetal cardiac rhabdomyoma in tuberous sclerosis.
unread.why: A prenatal TSC case demonstrates significant regression of a rapidly growing fetal cardiac rhabdomyoma with transplacental everolimus and continued postnatal treatment.

unread.title: Transplacental Sirolimus Therapy for Severe Fetal Cardiac Rhabdomyomas in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex: Organ-Specific Responses and 30-Month Follow-Up: A Case Report.
unread.why: The case provides tested prenatal and postnatal mTOR-inhibition strategies for severe TSC cardiac rhabdomyomas while documenting organ-specific responses and long-term outcomes.

unread.title: mTORC1 drives cell-autonomous astrocyte reactivity in tuberous sclerosis.
unread.why: Human brain organoids and patient tuber tissue establish a reusable model of TSC2-loss-driven reactive astrocytes and nominate astrocyte-specific therapeutic targets.

unread.title: Genes Do Not Read DSM: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex May Dominate with Multi-Neuropsychiatric Symptoms.
unread.why: The case shows that video EEG and brain imaging distinguish occult focal seizures from primary psychiatric symptoms and that lacosamide markedly reduced the seizures.

unread.title: Tuberous sclerosis complex diagnostic criteria update: recommendations of the 2012 Iinternational Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Consensus Conference.
unread.why: The consensus statement provides an evidence-based, clinically adopted framework for diagnosing TSC and guiding surveillance and treatment.

unread.title: Sirolimus for angiomyolipoma in tuberous sclerosis complex or lymphangioleiomyomatosis.
unread.why: A clinical trial provides direct evidence that sirolimus regresses TSC-associated angiomyolipomas and may improve lymphangioleiomyomatosis-associated lung function.

unread.title: Efficacy and safety of everolimus for subependymal giant cell astrocytomas associated with tuberous sclerosis complex (EXIST-1): a multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial.
unread.why: This randomized phase 3 trial demonstrated that everolimus substantially reduces TSC-associated subependymal giant cell astrocytomas.

unread.title: Cannabidiol (Epidyolex®) for severe behavioral manifestations in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex, mucopolysaccharidosis type III and fragile X syndrome: protocol for a series of randomized, placebo-controlled N-of-1 trials.
unread.why: This registered TSC trial protocol supplies a reusable design and outcome measures for testing cannabidiol against severe behavioral manifestations.

unread.title: A Review of Topical Sirolimus for the Treatment of Facial Angiofibromas in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
unread.why: The review reports clinical evidence that an FDA-approved topical sirolimus gel is a noninvasive treatment for TSC-associated facial angiofibromas.

unread.title: Molecular and Functional Assessment of TSC1 and TSC2 in Individuals with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
unread.why: The study validates molecular testing and functional assessment of TSC1/TSC2 variants for diagnosis and pathogenicity determination.

unread.title: Transplacental sirolimus: a new treatment strategy for life-threatening fetal cardiac rhabdomyomas-a case report.
unread.why: This TSC case report provides direct evidence that transplacental sirolimus can shrink fetal rhabdomyomas and improve severe fetal heart failure.

unread.title: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex: An updated in the treatment of epilepsy for early careers.
unread.why: The review consolidates multiple existing pharmacological, dietary, surgical, diagnostic, and monitoring strategies for TSC-associated epilepsy.

unread.title: Establishment of a human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) line from a patient harboring a TSC1 gene mutation.
unread.why: The paper establishes and characterizes a reusable patient-derived iPSC resource carrying a pathogenic TSC1 variant for mechanistic studies.

unread.title: Very low-dose Everolimus therapy diminishes cardiac tumours in tuberous sclerosis complex disease.
unread.why: This case report provides proof-of-concept that a very low everolimus trough level can regress TSC-associated cardiac tumors.

unread.title: Reversal of learning deficits in a Tsc2+/- mouse model of tuberous sclerosis.
unread.why: A TSC disease model directly demonstrates that short-term mTOR inhibition rescues synaptic-plasticity and learning deficits, supporting a reusable therapeutic strategy.

unread.title: Everolimus for angiomyolipoma associated with tuberous  sclerosis complex or sporadic lymphangioleiomyomatosis  (EXIST-2): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind,  placebo-controlled trial.
unread.why: A phase 3 randomized trial directly showed that everolimus reduces TSC-associated angiomyolipoma volume compared with placebo.

unread.title: Adjunctive everolimus therapy for treatment-resistant focal-onset seizures associated with tuberous sclerosis (EXIST-3): a phase 3, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
unread.why: A phase 3 trial in TSC demonstrated that adjunctive high- and low-exposure everolimus significantly reduces treatment-resistant focal seizure frequency versus placebo.

unread.title: Neurological and neuropsychiatric aspects of tuberous sclerosis complex.
unread.why: This disease-specific review identifies mTOR-inhibitor treatments, diagnostic criteria, and coordinated surveillance approaches for TSC neurological and systemic manifestations.

unread.title: Mutational and radiographic analysis of pulmonary disease consistent with lymphangioleiomyomatosis and micronodular pneumocyte hyperplasia in women with tuberous sclerosis.
unread.why: Prospective CT, pulmonary-function, and TSC2 genotyping data characterize and provide diagnostic biomarkers for pulmonary LAM/MMPH in women with TSC.

unread.title: Diagnosis of tuberous sclerosis complex.
unread.why: The paper provides clinically usable TSC consensus diagnostic criteria and explains how DNA testing complements diagnosis and enables prenatal or familial assessment.

unread.title: Genetic Etiologies, Diagnosis, and Treatment of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
unread.why: This TSC-focused review summarizes existing mTOR-inhibitor therapies and the genetic diagnostic and treatment framework relevant to TSC.

unread.title: Tuberous Sclerosis Consensus Conference: recommendations for diagnostic evaluation. National Tuberous Sclerosis Association.
unread.why: Consensus recommendations provide structured diagnostic testing and longitudinal surveillance for TSC patients and their families.

unread.title: Vigabatrin in the treatment of infantile spasms in tuberous sclerosis: literature review.
unread.why: The literature review reports high seizure-control rates with vigabatrin in TSC-associated infantile spasms and recommends it as first-line monotherapy.
